21-00-01-01.title: Environmental Control System Miscellaneous Cards (ECSMC) - Passenger
21-00-01-01.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated ECSMC is deactivated.
b. Both ARINC Signal Gateway cards in the opposite cardfile operate normally.
c. Opposite equipment cooling controller operates normally.
d. Opposite equipment cooling supply fan operates normally.
e. Opposite lavatory/galley fan operates normally.
f. One pack operates normally.
g. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
21-00-01-01.maintenanceNote:
NOTE: For a pack to be operating normally, certain items associated with that system must be operative. See MEL item 21-51-01 for a listing of those items.
1. Deactivate the inoperative ECSMC (AMM 21-00-00/901). NOTE 1: For left ECSMC deactivated: The left lower and forward upper recirculation fans are inoperative and the RECIRC FAN status message will be displayed. The aft cargo heat is inoperative and the CARGO HEAT AFT advisory message will be displayed. NOTE 2: For right ECSMC deactivated: The right lower and aft upper recirculation fans are inoperative and the RECIRC FAN status message will be displayed. The bulk cargo heat is inoperative and the CARGO HEAT BULK advisory message will be displayed.
21-00-01-01.companyMaintenanceNote: This MEL item has an impact on the carriage of temperature sensitive cargo /live animals. It is an ENG responsibility to advise the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO) of all defects affecting the carriage of cargo.
21-00-01-01.operationsNote:
1. For left ECSMC deactivated: A. Aft cargo heat is inoperative and the CARGO HEAT AFT advisory message will be displayed. B. Use MEL item 21-44-01 (O) Note for predicting aft cargo compartment temperatures. Temperature sensitive cargo should not be carried in the aft cargo compartment. NOTE: Actual aft cargo compartment temperature will not be available on the Air Synoptic. C. Left lower and forward upper recirculation fans are inoperative. Increase flight planning fuel by
0.7%.
2. For right ECSMC deactivated: A. Bulk cargo heat is inoperative and the CARGO HEAT BULK advisory message will be displayed. B. Use MEL item 21-44-03 (O) Note for predicting bulk cargo compartment temperatures. Temperature sensitive cargo should not be carried in the bulk cargo compartment. NOTE: Actual bulk cargo compartment temperature will not be available on the Air Synoptic. C. Right lower and aft upper recirculation fans are inoperative. Increase flight planning fuel by
0.7%.

21-25-01-01.title: Recirculation Fans - Passenger
21-25-01-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided associated recirculation fan is deactivated.
21-25-01-01.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the inoperative recirculation fan (AMM 21-00-00/901). NOTE: The RECIRC FAN status message indicates one or more fans are inoperative.
21-25-01-01.operationsNote:
Fuel penalties are negligible with one recirculation fan inoperative. For two recirculation fans inoperative, increase flight planning fuel by
0.7%, plus
0.3% for each additional inoperative fan.

21-29-05-01.remarks:

b. OFCR is considered inoperative.
21-29-05-01.maintenanceNote: NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 25-29-04. Deactivate the OFCR exhaust valve (AMM 21-00-00/901).

21-29-06-01.title: Overhead Flightcrew Rest Supply Shutoff Valves - Primary Supply Shutoff Valve
21-29-06-01.remarks:
a. Primary supply shutoff valve is deactivated closed.

21-29-06-01.operationsNote: With the primary shutoff valve disabled, the OFCR may become warm. To mitigate a warm OFCR, select a cooler flight deck area temperature. To mitigate the cooler flight deck temperature, the shoulder and foot heaters in the flight deck may be selected on.

21-29-06-02.title: Overhead Flightcrew Rest Supply Shutoff Valves - Secondary Supply Shutoff Valve
21-29-06-02.remarks:
a. Secondary supply shutoff valve is deactivated closed.
b. Primary supply shutoff valve operates normally.
c. Left air conditioning pack operates normally.
d. OFCR is not occupied at FL 250 or below.
21-29-06-02.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the secondary OFCR supply shutoff valve closed (AMM 21-00-00/901). NOTE: For a pack to be operating normally, certain items associated with that system must be operative. See MEL item 21-51-01 for a listing of those items.
21-29-06-02.operationsNote:
The OFCR is not available for in-flight use during taxi, takeoff and landing. Do not enter OFCR until altitude is above FL
250.

21-29-06-03.title: Overhead Flightcrew Rest Supply Shutoff Valves - Primary and Secondary Supply Shutoff Valves

21-31-01-01A.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Manual cabin pressure control is verified to operate normally on both outflow valves before each departure.
b. Left or right AFDC operates normally.
21-31-01-01A.maintenanceNote: Before each departure, verify manual cabin pressure control operates normally on both outflow valves (AMM 21-00-00/901).
21-31-01-01A.operationsNote: Leave OUTFLOW VALVE switches in AUTO unless required to accomplish a Non-Normal Checklist.

21-31-01-01B.title: Auto Cabin Pressure Controls (L and R) - One Outflow Valve Deactivated / Manual Control Operates on Other Valve
21-31-01-01B.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. One outflow valve is deactivated 7% open.
b. Manual cabin pressure control is verified to operate normally on the remaining outflow valve.
c. Left or right AFDC operates normally.
d. One pack operates normally, and the other pack operates normally or in standby cooling mode.
e. Both CTCs operate normally.
f. Both engine bleed systems operate normally.
g. For aft outflow valve deactivated 7% open, the OFCR and OFAR are considered inoperative.
21-31-01-01B.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the outflow valve 7% open and verify manual cabin pressure control operates normally on remaining outflow valve (AMM 21-00-00/901).
21-31-01-01B.operationsNote:
NOTE: For aft outflow valve deactivated, the airplane must also be
dispatched using MEL item 25-29-04.

1. Use MEL item 21-31-03-02 (O) procedure.
2. Leave OUTFLOW VALVE switches in AUTO unless required to accomplish a Non-Normal Checklist.

21-31-01-03.title: Auto Cabin Pressure Controls (L and R) - Unpressurized Flight
21-31-01-03.remarks:
a. Flight is conducted unpressurized.
b. Cargo compartments remain empty or contain only ballast, empty cargo handling equipment (ballast may be loaded in ULDs).
c. For extended overwater flight, manual cabin pressure control is verified to operate normally on both outflow valves.
d. The OFCR and OFAR are considered inoperative.
21-31-01-03.maintenanceNote: For extended overwater flight, verify manual cabin pressure control operates normally on both outflow valves (AMM 21-00-00/901).
21-31-01-03.companyMaintenanceNote: It is an ENG responsibility to advise the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO) of all defects affecting the carriage of cargo.
21-31-01-03.operationsNote:
NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 25-29-04.

1. Cargo compartments must remain empty, except for ballast, empty cargo containers (ballast may be loaded in ULDs), pallets, and cargo restraint components.
2. Position both outflow valves full open. A. Position both OUTFLOW VALVE switches to MAN. NOTE 1: The CABIN ALTITUDE AUTO caution message will be displayed. NOTE 2: Outflow valve position indications on EICAS may blank when MAN is selected. B. Hold each OUTFLOW VALVE MANUAL switch OPEN for 30 seconds.
3. Maintain the outflow valves full open unless required to accomplish a Non- Normal Checklist.
4. For flight with passengers: A. Limit enroute altitude to 10,000 feet. B. To avoid passenger discomfort, limit climb (after takeoff obstacle clearance has been assured) and descent rates to 500 fpm.

NOTE 2: A pack will operate in standby cooling mode with an inoperative ACM, or an inoperative ECV, or an inoperative Condenser Inlet Temperature Control System. e. Flight remains within 180 minutes of landing at a suitable airport.
24-11-01.maintenanceNote: Verify left, right and APU Generator Control Units (GCU) operate normally and disconnect the inoperative IDG (AMM 24-00-00/901). For GE: NOTE 1: During the authorized repair interval, if the associated engine is operated for more than 50 hours with the IDG disconnected, then the IDG should be removed for shop inspection prior to returning the airplane to service. NOTE 2: To prevent oil loss, cap the IDG/AGB seal pad drain if oil leakage beyond AMM allowable limits is observed from the engine drain mast, IDG/AGB port (AMM 71-71-00/601). For RR: NOTE: During the authorized repair interval, if the associated engine is operated for more than 50 hours with the IDG disconnected, then the IDG should be removed for shop inspection prior to returning the airplane to service.
24-11-01.operationsNote:
1. The flight must remain within 180 minutes of landing at a suitable airport.
2. Adjust flight planning fuel as follows: A. Increase flight planning fuel by
2.5% to account for the open APU air inlet door. B. Increase flight planning fuel by 90 kg per hour of APU usage inflight and 240 kg per hour of APU usage on the ground.
3. Verify the Backup AC electrical power system operates normally. Confirm the ELEC BACKUP SYS or ELEC BACKUP GEN L or R status and advisory messages are not displayed 30 seconds after both engines have been started.
4. Start the APU before departure and operate the APU continuously supplying the main AC bus associated with the inoperative IDG for the entire flight.

a. Seat is acceptable to the affected crewmember.
b. Repairs are made within 2 calendar days.

25-11-01-02-02B.title: Flight Crew Seats....................................2.25-11-01.1 - Powered Adjustment Operates Normally
25-11-01-02-02B.remarks: May be inoperative provided associated powered vertical adjustment system operates normally.

25-11-01-02-03.title: Flight Crew Seats....................................2.25-11-01.1 - Armrests
25-11-01-02-03.remarks:
a. Affected armrest is stowed in the retracted position or removed.
b. Seat is acceptable to affected crewmember.
25-11-01-02-03.maintenanceNote: Remove or stow the armrest in the retracted position (AMM 25-00-00/901).

25-11-01-02-04.title: Flight Crew Seats....................................2.25-11-01.1 - Lumbar/Thigh Supports
25-11-01-02-04.remarks: May be inoperative provided seat is acceptable to the affected crewmember.

25-11-01-02-05.title: Flight Crew Seats....................................2.25-11-01.1 - Headrests
25-11-01-02-05.remarks: May be inoperative provided seat is acceptable to the affected crewmember.

25-11-02-01A.title: Observer Seat(s).....................................2.25-11-02.1 - Passenger Seat Available
25-11-02-01A.remarks:
a. Seat is not required for operational reasons.
b. Repairs are made within 2 calendar days.

25-11-02-01B.title: Observer Seat(s).....................................2.25-11-02.1 - Second Observer Seat Available
25-11-02-01B.remarks:
a. Second observer seat is available, and acceptable for the performance of official duties.
b. Repairs are made within 2 calendar days.

25-11-02-01C.title: Observer Seat(s).....................................2.25-11-02.1 - Associated Safety Equipment Acceptable
25-11-02-01C.remarks:
a. Seat is not required for operational reasons.
b. Required minimum safety equipment (safety belt and oxygen) is available.
c. Repairs are made within 2 calendar days. NOTE: The Pilot-in-Command will determine if the minimum safety equipment is functional for the other persons authorized to occupy an observer seat(s).

25-11-02-02.title: Observer Seat(s).....................................2.25-11-02.1 - Second Observer Seat(s) (Including Associated Equipment)
25-11-02-02.remarks: NOTE: The Pilot-in-Command will determine if the minimum safety equipment is functional for the other persons authorized to occupy an observer seat(s).

25-18-01.title: Flotation Equipment
25-18-01.remarks:
Any in excess of those required may be inoperative or missing provided:
a. Seats with inoperative/missing life jacket are considered inoperative (Refer to item 25-25-02 Passenger Seats), and
b. The inoperative life jacket is removed from its stowage, placarded inoperative and placed out of sight so it cannot be mistaken for an operative unit, and
c. The SCCM is advised of the location of inoperative/missing equipment.
25-18-01.companyMaintenanceNote: Infant Flotation Devices carried onboard Aircraft Type Infant Life Jacket Baby Flotation Cot 777-300 20 4 777-300ER 24 8 NOTE: This information originates with ISD Operations Part B Cabin Crew Operating Manual.
25-18-01.operationsNote:
NOTE 1: One serviceable life jacket must be available for each occupant of
the aircraft.
NOTE 2: One serviceable Baby Floation Cot or Infant Lift Jacket must be
available for each infant below 2 years of age.
NOTE 3: MAINTENANCE - Make an entry in the logbook to remove the
stowed, inoperative life jacket at main base, recording the location
where inoperative units have been stowed.

25-20-01-01.title: Galley Equipment...................................2.25-20-01.1 - Ovens
25-20-01-01.remarks:
May be inoperative provided the following maintenance actions are performed.
a. Check and ensure the remaining ovens are serviceable.
b. Advise IOC if more than 3 ovens are unserviceable.
25-20-01-01.companyMaintenanceNote:
Carry out the following actions for each inoperative oven unit.
1. Check functionality of other ovens.
2. Notify IOC if more than 3 oven locations are inoperative.
3. In the Cabin Maintenance Operational Restrictions Field annotate the affected equipment as CI (Catering information).

25-20-01-03.title: Galley Equipment...................................2.25-20-01.1 - Chillers
25-20-01-03.companyMaintenanceNote:
1. Check functionality of the other chillers.
2. The galley catering equipment associated with the inoperative chiller(s) is loaded with dry ice.
3. Notify IOC if more than 3 chiller locations are inoperative.
4. In HKG notify IOC, in outstations notify the Airport Services Manager to coordinate dry ice uplift with the caterer.
5. In the Cabin Maintenance Log operational field restrictions field annotate the affected equipment as CI (Catering Information).
25-20-01-03.operationsNote:
NOTE: This passenger convenience/galley equipment item is not subject to
MEL regulatory policy. The rectification interval can be extended as
often as required without use of the regulatory Rectification Interval
Extension (RIE) policy.

25-20-01-05.title: Galley Equipment...................................2.25-20-01.1 - First Class Specialized Galley Equipment

25-24-01-01.title: Cabin Class Dividers.............................2.25-24-01.1 - J/PEY Cabin Divider (Panel Assy – window)
25-24-01-01.remarks: May be inoperative in the lowered position.

25-25-01-01A.title: Flight Attendant Seat Assembly (Single or Dual Position)..................................................2.25-25-01.1 - Passengers Carried
25-25-01-01A.remarks:
One seat position or assembly (dual position) may be inoperative provided:
a. Affected seat position or seat assembly is not occupied.
b. Flight attendant(s) displaced by inoperative seat(s) occupies either an adjacent flight attendant seat or the passenger seat which is listed in the Operations Procedure table.
c. Alternate procedures are established and used.
d. Folding type seat stows automatically or is secured in the retracted position.
e. Passenger seat assigned to flight attendant is placarded CREW SEAT ONLY. NOTE 1: An automatic folding seat that will not stow automatically is considered inoperative. NOTE 2: A seat position with an inoperative or missing restraint system is considered inoperative. NOTE 3: If one side of a dual seat assembly is inoperative and a flight attendant is displaced to the adjacent seat, the adjacent seat must operate normally.
25-25-01-01A.maintenanceNote: For automatic stowing inoperative, secure seat in stowed position (AMM 25-00-00/901).
25-25-01-01A.companyMaintenanceNote:
1. Placard the affected seat: "DO NOT OCCUPY" (Placard P/N DNO1).
2. Install strap assembly on the passenger seat assigned to attendant(s): CREW SEAT ONLY. (P/N G25B2016-18).
25-25-01-01A.operationsNote: Alternate procedures require that the flight attendant assigned to the affected seat must occupy the alternate passenger seat identified in the following table: 777-300 (773P) Inoperative seat Alternate seat location L1 11D R1 11G L2 FWD 18C R2 FWD 18H L3 54A R3 54K L4 67C R4 67H L5 AFT O/B 80D R5 AFT O/B 80G 777-300ER (773A) Inoperative seat Alternate seat location L1 FWD 12D R1 1K L2 FWD 15A R2 16K L3 31A R3 30G L4 59A R4 59K L5 O/B 72C R5 O/B 72G 777-300ER (773K) Inoperative seat Alternate seat location L1 FWD 11A R1 11K L2 FWD 19A R2 19K L3 43A R3 43K L4 59A R4 59K L5 O/B 72D R5 O/B 72G 777-300ER (773J) Inoperative seat Alternate seat location L1 FWD 11A R1 FWD 11K L2 FWD R2 AFT (if vacant) or 19A L2 AFT R2 AFT (if vacant) or 19A R2 FWD R2 AFT (if vacant) or 19K* L3 39A R3 39K L4 59A R4 59K L5 O/B 72D R5 O/B 72G R5 I/B 72G * For DV requirements: If R2 FWD is INOP, crew seated in L2 AFT will also be relocated to seat 35D.

25-25-01-01B.title: Flight Attendant Seat Assembly (Single or Dual Position)..................................................2.25-25-01.1 - No Passengers Carried
25-25-01-01B.remarks:
a. No passengers are carried.
b. Folding type seat stows automatically or is secured in the retracted position.
c. Affected seat position or seat assembly is not occupied.
d. Alternate procedures are established and used. NOTE 1: An automatic folding seat that will not stow automatically is considered inoperative. NOTE 2: A seat position with an inoperative or missing restraint system is considered inoperative.
25-25-01-01B.maintenanceNote: For automatic stowing inoperative, secure seat in stowed position (AMM 25-00-00/901).
25-25-01-01B.operationsNote:
1. No passengers may be carried.
2. Alternate procedures require that the affected flight attendants occupy a passenger seat.

25-25-01-02.title: Flight Attendant Seat Assembly (Single or Dual Position)..................................................2.25-25-01.1 - Non-Required Flight Attendant Seats
25-25-01-02.remarks:
a. Affected seat position or seat assembly is not occupied.
b. Folding type seat stows automatically or is secured in the retracted position. NOTE 1: An automatic folding seat that will not stow automatically is considered inoperative. NOTE 2: A seat position with an inoperative or missing restraint system is considered inoperative.
25-25-01-02.maintenanceNote: For automatic stowing inoperative, secure seat in stowed position (AMM 25-00-00/901).
25-25-01-02.companyMaintenanceNote: Placard the affected seat (if not removed): “DO NOT OCCUPY” (Placard P/N DNO1). COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE 777-300 (773P) Inoperative seat Alternate seat location L2 AFT 18C R2 AFT 18H L5 FWD 80D L5 AFT I/B 80D L5 CENTRE 80D R5 FWD 80G R5 AFT I/B 80G R5 CENTRE 80G 777-300ER (773A) Inoperative seat Alternate seat location L1 AFT 12D L2 AFT 15A L5 I/B 72C R5 FWD 72G R5 I/B 72G 777-300ER (773K) Inoperative seat Alternate seat location L1 AFT 11A L2 AFT 19A L5 I/B 72D R5 FWD 72G R5 I/B 72G 777-300ER (773J) Inoperative seat Alternate seat location L1 AFT 11A R2 AFT 19K L5 I/B 72D

25-25-02-01.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - Passenger Seats (includes all Configurations and Locations)
25-25-02-01.remarks:
a. Seat does not block an emergency exit.
b. Seat does not restrict any passenger from access to the main airplane aisle.
c. Affected seat(s) is blocked and placarded DO NOT OCCUPY. NOTE 1: A seat with an inoperative seat belt or shoulder harness is considered inoperative. NOTE 2: Affected seat(s) may include the seat(s) behind and/or adjacent outboard seats. NOTE 3: Inoperative seats do not affect the required number of flight attendants.
25-25-02-01.companyMaintenanceNote:
1. Placard the affected seat 'DO NOT OCCUPY' (Placard P/N DNO1).
2. In the Cabin Operations Restrictions Field annotate the affected seat as NS (No Sell) and notify the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO).

25-25-02-02A.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - Seat Secured
25-25-02-02A.remarks: May be inoperative and seat occupied provided seat is secured in the taxi, takeoff, and landing (TTL) position.
25-25-02-02A.maintenanceNote: Secure the associated seat in the taxi, takeoff, and landing (TTL) position (AMM 25-00-00/901).
25-25-02-02A.companyMaintenanceNote: In the Cabin Maintenance Operational Restrictions Filed, annotate the affected seat as SL (Sell last) and notify the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO).

25-25-02-02B.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - Seat Immovable
25-25-02-02B.remarks: May be inoperative and seat occupied provided seat is immovable in the taxi, takeoff, and landing (TTL) position.

25-25-02-03.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - Underseat Baggage Restraining System
25-25-02-03.remarks:
a. Baggage is not stowed under seat with inoperative restraining bar.
b. Associated seat is placarded DO NOT STOW BAGGAGE UNDER THIS SEAT.
c. Procedures are established to alert cabin crew of inoperative restraining bar.
25-25-02-03.operationsNote: Alternate procedures require that the SCCM is made aware of the requirement not to stow baggage under the affected seat(s) and notifies affected passengers accordingly.

25-25-02-04-01.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - With Seat Positioning Controls for Taxi, Takeoff, and Landing (TTL) and/or Other Controls
25-25-02-04-01.remarks:
May be inoperative or missing and seat occupied provided:
a. Armrest does not block an Emergency Exit.
b. Armrest does not restrict any passenger from access to the main airplane aisle.
c. If armrest is missing, seat is secured in the full upright position.
25-25-02-04-01.maintenanceNote: If required, secure the associated seat in the upright position (AMM 25-00-00/901).
25-25-02-04-01.companyMaintenanceNote: In the Cabin Maintenance Operational Restrictions Filed, annotate the affected seat as SL (Sell Last) and notify the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO).

25-25-02-04-02.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - Without Seat Positioning Controls for Taxi, Takeoff, and Landing (TTL) and/or Other Controls
25-25-02-04-02.remarks:
May be inoperative or missing and seat occupied provided:
a. Armrest does not block an Emergency Exit.
b. Armrest does not restrict any passenger from access to the main airplane aisle.
c. For 777-300ER Business Class Seat, armrest must be locked in down position.
25-25-02-04-02.companyMaintenanceNote:
1. For 777-300ER Business Class Seat on 773A and 773K configuration, armrest must be locked in down position. Refer to MMB 4-25-TDM154- B777 for lockout procedure.
2. For 777-300ER Business Class Seat on 773J configuration, armrest must be locked in down position. Refer to MMB 4-25-TDM953-B777 for lockout procedure.
3. For other classes, in the Cabin Maintenance Operational Restrictions Filed, annotate the affected seat as SL (Sell Last) and notify the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO).

25-25-02-05.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - Foot Rest / Leg Rest
25-25-02-05.remarks:
May be damaged or missing provided:
a. Foot rest / leg rest does not block an emergency exit.
b. Foot rest / leg rest does not restrict any passenger from access to the aisle.
25-25-02-05.companyMaintenanceNote: In the Cabin Maintenance Operational Restrictions Filed, annotate the affected seat as SL (Sell Last) and notify the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO).

25-25-02-06-01.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - Seat Belt Air Bags Required
25-25-02-06-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided affected seat is blocked and placarded DO NOT OCCUPY.
25-25-02-06-01.companyMaintenanceNote:
1. Placard affected seat DO NOT OCCUPY (PLACARD P/N DNO1).
2. In the Cabin Maintenance Operations Restrictions Field, annotate the affected seat as NS (No Sell) and notify the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO).

25-25-02-07.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - Headrest
25-25-02-07.companyMaintenanceNote: In the Cabin Maintenance Operations Restrictions Field, annotate the affected seat as SL (Sell Last) and notify the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO).

25-25-02-08.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - Meal Tray
25-25-02-08.remarks:
May be damaged and seat occupied provided:
a. The meal tray is safe for normal usage.
25-25-02-08.companyMaintenanceNote: In the Cabin Maintenance Operations Restrictions Field, annotate the affected seat as SL (Sell Last) and notify the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO).

25-25-02-09.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - Electrical / Electronic Systems / Components
25-25-02-09.remarks:
May be inoperative and seat occupied provided:
a. Associated system(s) / component(s) is/are deactivated.
b. Where appropriate, mechanical backup system operates normally.
25-25-02-09.companyMaintenanceNote:
1. For inoperative seat electric / electronic system(s) / component(s), use the appropriate established associated deactivation procedures for the inoperative components.
2. In the Cabin Maintenance Operational Restrictions Filed, annotate the affected seat as SL (Sell Last) and notify the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO).

25-25-02-13.title: Passenger Seats....................................2.25-25-02.1 - In Flight Entertainment System (IFE)
25-25-02-13.companyMaintenanceNote: In the Cabin Maintenance Operations Restrictions Field, annotate the affected seat as SL (Sell Last) and notify the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO).

25-25-04.title: Crew Rest Seats (OFCR)
25-25-04.remarks:
a. Seat is not occupied.
b. Affected seat(s) is blocked and placarded DO NOT OCCUPY. NOTE: A seat with an inoperative seat belt is considered inoperative.
25-25-04.companyMaintenanceNote: Placard the affected seat “DO NOT OCCUPY (Placard P/N DNO1).

25-25-04-01A.title: Crew Rest Seats (OFCR).......................2.25-25-04.1 - Seat Secured Up-Right
25-25-04-01A.remarks: May be inoperative and seat occupied provided seat is secured in the full up- right position.
25-25-04-01A.maintenanceNote: Secure the associated seat in the upright position (AMM 25-00-00/901).

25-25-04-01B.title: Crew Rest Seats (OFCR).......................2.25-25-04.1 - Immovable Seat Back
25-25-04-01B.remarks: May be inoperative and seat occupied provided seat back is immovable in the full up-right position.

25-25-04-02.title: Crew Rest Seats (OFCR).......................2.25-25-04.1 - Armrests
25-25-04-02.remarks: May be inoperative provided armrest is stowed in retracted position or removed.
25-25-04-02.maintenanceNote: Stow an inoperative armrest in the retracted position or remove the armrest (AMM 25-00-00/901).

25-25-04-03.title: Crew Rest Seats (OFCR).......................2.25-25-04.1 - Leg Rests
25-25-04-03.remarks:
May be inoperative and seat occupied provided:
a. Leg rest is stowed in the retracted position.
b. Seat is acceptable to the affected crewmember.
25-25-04-03.maintenanceNote: Stow an inoperative leg rest in the retracted position or remove the leg rest. (AMM 25-00-00/901).

25-25-06-01A.title: Passenger Mini-Suites...........................2.25-25-06.1 - Passenger Carried
25-25-06-01A.remarks: One or more may be inoperative and seat occupied provided the affected door(s) is secured in the fully open position or removed.
25-25-06-01A.maintenanceNote: Secure the affected door open (AMM 25-00-00/901 TR 25-296).

25-25-06-01B.title: Passenger Mini-Suites...........................2.25-25-06.1 - No Passenger Carried
25-25-06-01B.remarks:
One or more may be inoperative provided:
a. Affected seat is not occupied, and
b. Affected seat is considered inoperative.
25-25-06-01B.companyMaintenanceNote:
1. Placard the affected seat “DO NOT OCCUPY (Placard P/N DNO1).
2. In the Cabin Operations Restrictions Field annotate the affected seat as NS (No Sell) and notify the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO). ATA 25 Section

25-28-01A.title: Storage Bin(s)/Cabin, Galley and Lavatory Storage Compartments/ Closets....................................................2.25-28-01.1 - Secured Closed
25-28-01A.remarks:
a. Procedures are established to secure the affected bin, compartment or closet in the closed position,
b. Associated bin, compartment or closet is prominently placarded UNSERVICEABLE, DO NOT USE,
c. Any emergency equipment located in affected bin, compartment or closet is considered inoperative.
d. Affected bin, compartment or closet is not used for storage of any items except for those permanently affixed. NOTE 1: For overhead bins, if no partitions are installed, the entire overhead bin is considered inoperative. NOTE 2: Proviso is not intended to preclude crewmember inspections.
25-28-01A.maintenanceNote: Secure and placard inoperative bins, compartments or closets closed (AMM 25-00-00/901).
25-28-01A.companyMaintenanceNote:
1. Placard the applicable bin/compartment with security seal tape (P/N F002356) at a location readily visable to Cabin Crew.
2. Placard the applicable bin/compartment "UNSERVICEABLE, PLEASE DO NOT USE" (P/N 4B11Q4029-1). NOTE: Ensure the "UNSERVICEABLE, PLEASE DO NOT USE" placard does not overlap the security seal tape.
25-28-01A.operationsNote: For emergency equipment located in affected compartment, the airplane must also be dispatched using the applicable emergency equipment MEL item.

25-28-01B.title: Storage Bin(s)/Cabin, Galley and Lavatory Storage Compartments/ Closets....................................................2.25-28-01.1 - Door Removed or Retractable Door Secured Open
25-28-01B.remarks:
a. For non-retractable doors, affected door is removed.
b. For retractable doors, affected door is removed or secured in the retracted (fully open) position.
c. Affected bin, compartment or closet is not used for storage of any items, except those permanently affixed.
d. Affected bin, compartment or closet is prominently placarded UNSERVICEABLE, DO NOT USE.
e. Procedures are established and used to alert crew members and passengers of inoperative bins, compartments or closets.
f. Passengers are briefed that affected bin, compartment or closet is not to be used. NOTE 1: For overhead bins, if no partitions are installed, the entire overhead bin is considered inoperative. NOTE 2: Any emergency equipment located in the affected bin, compartment or closet (permanently affixed) is available for use.
25-28-01B.maintenanceNote: Remove affected door and placard associated bin, compartment or closet (AMM 25-00-00/901).
25-28-01B.companyMaintenanceNote: Placard the applicable bin/compartment "UNSERVICEABLE, PLEASE DO NOT USE" (P/N 4B11Q4029-1).
25-28-01B.operationsNote: Ensure crew members and passengers are briefed that associated bin, compartment or closet is not used.

25-28-01C.title: Storage Bin(s)/Cabin, Galley and Lavatory Storage Compartments/ Closets....................................................2.25-28-01.1 - Closed
25-28-01C.remarks:
a. Affected bin, compartment, or closet is closed.
b. Affected bin, compartment, or closet is prominently placarded “DO NOT USE”.
c. Any emergency equipment located in affected bin, compartment, or closet is considered inoperative.
d. Location placarding for any emergency equipment stored in affected bin, compartment, or closet is removed or obscured. NOTE: Does not preclude opening of the associated compartment by crew for required security checks.
25-28-01C.companyMaintenanceNote: Placard the applicable bin/compartment "UNSERVICEABLE, PLEASE DO NOT USE" (P/N 4B11Q4029-1).

25-28-01-01.title: Storage Bin(s)/Cabin, Galley and Lavatory Storage Compartments/ Closets....................................................2.25-28-01.1 - Multi Latch/Quarter Turn Lug Installations
25-28-01-01.remarks:
One latch/lug per compartment may be inoperative provided:
a. Remaining latch(es)/lug(s) on affected compartments operates normally.
b. If affected compartment is used for a galley cart, the cart remains empty.

25-29-03.title: Overhead Flight Crew/Attendant Rest Door
25-29-03.remarks: May be inoperative provided associated crew/attendant rest is considered inoperative.
25-29-03.operationsNote: NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 25-29-04.

25-29-03-01.title: Overhead Flight Crew/ Attendant Rest Door .............................2.25-29-03.1 - Door Lock
25-29-03-01.remarks:
a. Associated OFCR/OFAR door lock is deactivated in the unlocked position.
b. Associated OFCR/OFAR door opens and closes normally.
25-29-03-01.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the OFCR/OFAR door lock in the unlocked position (AMM 25-00-00/901). For keyless lock installed, the lock assembly override may be used, or the lock assembly may be removed.
25-29-03-01.companyMaintenanceNote:
If installed, the Lock Assembly Override Feature may be used to deactivate the door lock.
1. Remove cover plate covering override feature. Cover plate is located on inside top of door.
2. Remove rod assembly by unscrewing the rod assembly nut.
3. Lower the horizontal plate supported by the spring to disengage the bolt from the strike.
4. Verify the door can be opened and closed normally from both sides.

25-29-04A.title: Crew/Attendant Rest Facilities (OFCR, OFAR)........................2.25-29-04.1 - Deactivated Closed
25-29-04A.remarks: a. Associated crew/attendant rest is deactivated closed. NOTE: This provision is not intended to prohibit crew/attendant rest inspections by crewmembers.
25-29-04A.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the associated crew/attendant rest closed AMM 25-00-00/901).
25-29-04A.companyMaintenanceNote: Placard the applicable bin/compartment "UNSERVICEABLE, PLEASE DO NOT USE" (P/N 4B11Q4029-1). COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE Flights involving Ultra Long Range/Extended Flight Duty Period will be affected. Refer to OM-A (Approved Flight Time Limitations Scheme).

25-29-04-01.title: Crew/Attendant Rest Facilities (OFCR, OFAR)........................2.25-29-04.1 - Bunks
25-29-04-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided bunk is not occupied. NOTE: A bunk with an inoperative or missing restraint system is considered inoperative.
25-29-04-01.operationsNote:
COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE
Flights involving Ultra Long Range/Extended Flight Duty Period will be affected .
Refer to OM-A (Approved Flight Time Limitations Scheme).

25-30-01.title: Galley/Cabin Waste Container Access Door/Covers
25-30-01.remarks:
a. Associated waste container is empty and access is secured to prevent waste introduction into the waste container.
b. Procedures are established to ensure that sufficient galley/cabin waste containers are available to accommodate all waste that may be generated on a flight.
25-30-01.maintenanceNote: Empty the receptacle and secure the access door/cover in a manner that will prevent waste from being deposited in the waste compartment/receptacle (AMM 25-00-00/901).
25-30-01.companyMaintenanceNote: Annotate the cabin maintenance log ZADD entry with the following statement: “The SCCM is to ensure that sufficient galley/cabin waste containers are available to accommodate all waste that may be generated on the flight”.

25-40-01.title: Interior Lavatory Door Ashtrays
25-40-01.remarks:
One or more may be inoperative or missing provided:
a. Associated lavatory door is locked closed and placarded, INOPERATIVE - DO NOT ENTER.
b. Associated lavatory is used only by crewmembers. NOTE 1: These provisions are not intended to prohibit lavatory use or inspections by crewmembers. NOTE 2: In the event of any lavatory being locked closed, the airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 25-45-01.

25-41-01-01.title: Exterior Lavatory Door Ashtrays..................................................2.25-41-01.1 - Passenger
25-41-01-01.remarks: Fifty percent may be inoperative or missing provided repairs are made within 10 calendar days.

25-41-02.title: Lavatory Waste Container Flapper/Access Doors
25-41-02.remarks:
a. Associated waste container is empty and access is secured to prevent waste introduction into the waste container.
b. Lavatory is used only by crewmembers.
c. Associated lavatory entrance door is locked closed and placarded, INOPERATIVE - DO NOT ENTER. NOTE: These provisions are not intended to prohibit lavatory use or inspections by crewmembers.
25-41-02.maintenanceNote: Empty waste container, secure container access and close and lock lavatory door (AMM 25-00-00/901).
25-41-02.operationsNote:
NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL 25-45-01.

Lavatory door should remain locked closed, except for use or inspection by crewmembers.

25-45-01.title: Lavatory
25-45-01.remarks:
One or more may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated lavatory door is locked closed and placarded INOPERATIVE - DO NOT ENTER, and
b. Operation of remaining toilets is checked before each departure. NOTE: These provisions are not intended to prohibit inspections by crewmembers.
25-45-01.companyMaintenanceNote:
1. Secure closed and appropriately placard the associated lavatory doors.
2. Alert IOC immediately for any dispatch with multiple toilets inoperative.
3. Advise SCCM of the inoperative lavatory positions. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE Guidance on recommended minimum toilet/passenger ratio for dispatch: Configuration Recommended Minimum Toilet/Passenger Ratio A/C Without FCL JCL PEY/YCL 1:60 A/C With FCL FCL JCL PEY/YCL 1:20 1:60 The recommended minimum Toilet/Passenger ratio is provided to assist the Captain and the SCCM, in coordination with IOC, in making dispatch decisions. They are recommendations, not limitations. If the number of available lavatories does not achieve the required ratio, IOC, Commander, and SCCM are to discuss and agree on the options on a case by case (e.g., continue operations, tech stop or pax offload based on sector length). NOTE: Dispatch decision from HKG should also consider the return flight. Passenger offload shall only be considered as a last resort.

25-52-01.title: Lower Cargo Compartment Lining (Forward and Aft)
25-52-01.remarks: May be damaged or missing provided procedures are established and used to verify the associated cargo compartment remains empty or contains only ballast, empty cargo handling equipment (ballast may be loaded in ULDs), or fly away kits.
25-52-01.companyMaintenanceNote: It is an ENG responsibility to advise the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO) of all defects affecting the carriage of cargo.
25-52-01.operationsNote:
NOTE: Lower Cargo Compartment Linings include: sloping sidewall liners, all
endwalls, decompression panels, ceiling liners and mounted
equipment, all cargo door liners, vertical sidewall liners including
cheek panels and mounted equipment, waste tank enclosure panels,
access panels, ceiling light assemblies, the main equipment center
bulkhead liner, firestops, bilge curtains, bulkhead liners, endwall/
enclosure liners and panels, and all fasteners attaching cargo linings.
In addition, some of the cargo floor panels and walkways are included
in this item because they are containment barriers for smoke and fire
suppression. The forward cargo compartment floor panels and
walkways that are containment barriers are located at the aft end of
the forward compartment. The aft compartment floor panels and
walkways that are containment barriers are located at the aft end of
the aft compartment, just forward of the bulk cargo compartment. All of
the bulk cargo compartment floor panels are containment barriers.

The associated cargo compartment must remain empty, except for ballast, empty cargo containers (ballast may be loaded in ULDs), pallets, and cargo restraint components. NOTE: Both the aft and bulk cargo compartments must remain empty when there are damaged or missing linings in either the aft or the bulk cargo compartment.

25-53-01.title: Lower Cargo Handling Systems
25-53-01.remarks: NOTE: Any portion of the system which operates normally may be used.
25-53-01.companyMaintenanceNote:

3.6.
2. It is an ENG responsibility to advise the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO) of all defects affecting the carriage of cargo.
3. Deactivation procedures for most cargo restraint or cargo guiding equipment are either obvious (e.g. inoperative container stop needs to be released to retracted position or removed to prevent interference with cargo loading) or unnecessary (e.g., a damaged end stop can be left as is). Consequently, no procedures are listed in this MEL.
25-53-02A.operationsNote:
NOTE: Do not use the cargo compartment if the number of inoperative or
missing restraints is more than specified in the CX Aircraft Handling
Manual. Refer to MEL Item 25-53-02B.

MAINTENANCE NOTE

airplane structure (sill chord/web, or sill chord/web/stub-frame) must

length bolt if required, or replace bolt with shorter grip length. (AMM
25-00-00/901)
NOTE 2: The cargo handling system left and right BL 6.5, 19.5, 41.5 and 58.5
roller trays must remain installed to stabilize cargo floor beams and
frames.

25-53-02C.companyMaintenanceNote:
1. Coordination with the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO) required to identify the equipment locations and to establish any required load limitations based on the information provided in the CX Aircraft Handling Manual Part B, Chapter 3,
3.6.
2. It is an ENG responsibility to advise the Turnaround Coordinator of all defects affecting the carriage of cargo.
25-53-02C.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
NOTE 1: The cargo handling system doorsill hardware must be installed for
flight. If hardware is missing, fasteners common to the doorsill and
airplane structure (sill chord/web, or sill chord/web/stub-frame) must
be reinstalled prior to flight. Use additional washers with existing grip
length bolt if required, or replace bolt with shorter grip length. (AMM
25-00-00/901)
NOTE 2: The cargo handling system left and right BL 6.5, 19.5, 41.5 and 58.5

26-17-01A.remarks:
a. Both wheel well fire detection loops are deactivated.

26-17-01B.remarks:
May be inoperative provided :
a. Both wheel well fire detection loops are deactivated.
b. Landing gear remains extended for ten minutes after takeoff.
c. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied. NOTE 1: Avoid the possibility of retracting an overheated wheel by leaving landing gear extended for ten minutes after takeoff. NOTE 2: In case of engine failure after V1, landing gear should be retracted until takeoff obstacles are cleared.
26-17-01B.maintenanceNote:
1. Deactivate wheel well fire detection loops 1 and 2 (AMM DDG 26-00-00/901).
2. Ensure brakes are cool to the touch prior to engine start (AMM 26-00-00/901).
26-17-01B.operationsNote:
1. It is not necessary to apply landing gear extended takeoff performance adjustments when dispatching under this item.
2. In case of engine failure after V1, landing gear should be retracted until takeoff obstacles are cleared.
3. Increase flight planning fuel by 2,041 kg to account for the landing gear extended for ten minutes after takeoff.
4. Leave landing gear extended for 10 minutes after takeoff. For engine failure after V1, retract landing gear until obstacles are cleared. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT item.

b. Metered bottle 2A operates normally.
c. Associated bottle is deactivated.
d. Airplane is operated pressurized.
e. Appropriate flight planning adjustments are applied to account for remaining fire suppression capability. See Operations Procedure.
26-23-01-03.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the inoperative fire extinguishing bottle (AMM 26-00-00/901).
26-23-01-03.operationsNote:
For EDTO flight planning, use the following total fire suppression times for planning.
1. 777-300s have three metered bottles installed (2A, 2B, and 2C): NOTE: Bottles 1A, 1B and 2A must operate normally. One Bottle Inoperative Two Bottles Inoperative (2B or 2C) (2B and 2C) Limit EDTO planning to 120 Limit EDTO planning to 60 minutes. minutes.

One Bottle Inop Two Bottles Inop Three Bottles Inop (2B or 2C) (2B and 2C) (2B, 2C and 2D) Limit EDTO planning Limit EDTO planning Limit EDTO planning to 180 minutes. to 120 minutes. to 60 minutes.

26-23-01-04.title: Lower Cargo Compartment Fire Extinguisher Bottles..............................2.26-23-01.1 - Bottle Pressure Switches
26-23-01-04.remarks:
a. Associated bottle is verified full.
b. Associated bottle squib firing circuit is verified operating normally before each departure.
26-23-01-04.maintenanceNote: Verify the associated bottle is full and verify the associated squib operates normally before each departure (AMM26-00-00/901). NOTE: For a bottle pressure switch failed closed when the bottle pressure is normal or the bottle pressure is low, or the bottle squib fails a squib test, the associated bottle status message will be displayed.

26-23-02A.title: Lower Cargo Compartment Fire Extinguisher Flow Valves (Forward or Aft)......................................2.26-23-02.1 - One Inoperative
26-23-02A.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated flow valve is capped.
b. Associated flow valve squib electrical connectors are capped and stowed.
c. The associated cargo compartment remains empty or contains only ballast, empty cargo handling equipment (ballast may be loaded in ULDs).
26-23-02A.companyMaintenanceNote: It is an ENG responsibility to advise the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO) of all defects affecting the carriage of cargo.
26-23-02A.operationsNote: 1. The associated lower cargo compartment must remain empty, except for ballast, empty cargo containers (ballast may be loaded in ULDs), pallets, and cargo restraint components.

26-23-02B.title: Lower Cargo Compartment Fire Extinguisher Flow Valves (Forward or Aft)......................................2.26-23-02.1 - Both Inoperative
26-23-02B.remarks: a. Procedures are established and used to verify cargo compartments remain empty or contain only ballast, empty cargo handling equipment (ballast may be loaded in ULDs).
26-23-02B.maintenanceNote: 1. Lower cargo compartments must remain empty, except for ballast, empty cargo containers (ballast may be loaded in ULDs), pallets, and cargo restraint components.
26-23-02B.companyMaintenanceNote: It is an ENG responsibility to advise the Turnaround Coordinator (TCO) of all defects affecting the carriage of cargo.
26-23-02B.operationsNote: 1. The lower cargo compartments must remain empty, except for ballast, empty cargo containers (ballast may be loaded in ULDs), pallets, and cargo restraint components.

26-24-01-01A.title: Lavatory Fire Extinguisher Systems...........................2.26-24-01.1 - Smoke Detection System(s) Operative
26-24-01-01A.remarks: May be inoperative for each lavatory provided associated lavatory smoke detection system operates normally.

26-24-01-01B.title: Lavatory Fire Extinguisher Systems...........................2.26-24-01.1 - Smoke Detection System(s) Inoperative
26-24-01-01B.remarks:
May be inoperative for each lavatory provided associated:
a. Lavatory waste container is empty.
b. Lavatory door is locked closed and placarded, INOPERATIVE - DO NOT ENTER.
c. Lavatory is used only by crewmembers. NOTE: These provisions are not intended to prohibit lavatory use or inspections by crewmembers.
26-24-01-01B.operationsNote:
NOTE: Aircraft must also be dispatched using MEL item 25-45-01.

Lavatory door should remain locked closed, except for use or inspection by crewmembers.

26-26-01.title: Portable Fire Extinguishers (Cabin)
26-26-01.remarks:
Any in excess of those required may be inoperative or missing provided:
a. At least one portable fire extinguisher is located in the cockpit.
b. At least six portable fire extinguishers are located in the cabin.
c. At least three of the required handheld fire extinguishers in the passenger cabin shall contain HALON (BCF), or it's equivalent, as the extinguishing agent.
d. For -300ER, at least one portable fire extinguisher is located in the OFCR.
e. For -300ER, at least one portable fire extinguisher is located in the OFAR.
f. Required distribution is maintained.
26-26-01.companyMaintenanceNote:
1. The aircraft may continue the flight or series of flights but shall not depart Hong Kong if it is reasonably practicable for repairs or replacements to be carried out.
2. Required portable fire extinguishers in the flight deck, OFCR, and OFAR are in addition to the six portable fire extinguishers required in the cabin. For a 777-300ER, a total of nine portable fire extinguishers are required. For a 777-300, a total of seven portable fire extinguishers are required. 2AB.TO2A7D 2Y7-FLOW Section 2 Table of Contents ATA 27
26-26-01.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
1. Ensure inoperative fire extinguisher remains in the installed location until
removed from the aircraft at the next suitable maintenance facility.
2. Obscure or remove location placarding from the inoperative fire
extinguisher.
3. Ensure required distribution of serviceable extinguishers is maintained
throughout the airplane.

27-00-01.title: Flight Controls Synoptic Display
27-00-01.operationsNote: For missing data on the Synoptic Display, selecting an alternate location for the display (L INBD, LWR CTR, or R INBD) may restore the missing data. Synoptic Displays containing missing data may continue to be used to the extent remaining data is useful. Airplane system faults will be annunciated by alerting and status messages.

27-02-03.title: Primary Flight Computer Channels
27-02-03.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative PFC channel is deactivated.
b. Operations are limited to three flights before repairs are made.
c. Approach minimums do not require its use.
d. Airplane does not depart HKG.
27-02-03.maintenanceNote: Determine which PFC channel is inoperative, then deactivate the inoperative channel (AMM 27-00-00/901). NOTE: FLIGHT CONTROL SYS may display with hydraulics depressurized. Pressurize hydraulics and assure FLIGHT CONTROL SYS does not display for dispatch.
27-02-03.operationsNote:
NOTE: Airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 22-11-07-01.

The NO LAND 3 advisory message will be displayed.

27-02-04.title: PFCS Interface
27-02-04.remarks: May be inoperative provided landing gear truck tilt pressure is verified to be normal before each departure.
27-02-04.maintenanceNote: Verify truck tilt pressure is normal before each departure (AMM 27-00-00/901).
27-02-04.operationsNote:
NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item
22-11-07-01.

The NO LAND 3 advisory message may be displayed.

27-02-05.title: Actuator Pressure Sensors
27-02-05.remarks: One flaperon or rudder sensor may be inoperative.

27-02-06.title: Flight Control Hydraulic Shutoff Valve Systems
27-02-06.remarks: May be inoperative provided the associated valve is deactivated open.
27-02-06.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the associated hydraulic shutoff valve (SOV) in the open position (AMM 27-00-00/901). NOTE: The flight control hydraulic shutoff valve system includes the SOV and associated VALVE CLOSED light and FLT CONTROL VALVE advisory message.

27-02-08-01-02.title: Thrust Asymmetry Compensation (TAC) Function .................................................2.27-02-08.1 - AUTO Light

27-03-01.title: Flap/Slat Control Lanes
27-03-01.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Flap lever control position sensor is verified to operate normally.
b. Alternate control is verified to operate normally before each departure.
27-03-01.maintenanceNote: Verify the flap lever control position sensor operates normally, and before each departure, verify the alternate control for the flaps and slats operates normally. (AMM 27-00-00/901).

27-03-02.title: Flap Secondary Control
27-03-02.remarks: May be inoperative provided Slat Secondary Control is verified to operate normally.
27-03-02.maintenanceNote: Verify Slat Secondary Control operates normally (AMM 27-00-00/901).

27-03-03.title: Slat Secondary Control
27-03-03.remarks: May be inoperative provided Flap Secondary Control is verified to operate normally.
27-03-03.maintenanceNote: Verify Flap Secondary Control operates normally (AMM 27-00-00/901).

27-11-01.title: Aileron Trim System
27-11-01.remarks:
a. Aileron trim system is deactivated.
b. Aileron trim system is verified to be centered before departure.
c. Autopilot roll modes operate normally.
27-11-01.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the aileron trim system (AMM 27-00-00/901). NOTE: For autopilot roll modes to operate normally, the following items must operate normally: MEL Item Associated Status Message

27-11-03-01.title: Aileron Power Control Units (PCUs)............................................2.27-11-03.1 - Passenger
27-11-03-01.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative PCU is deactivated in the bypass mode.
b. Inoperative PCU blocking mode is verified to operate normally.
c. Ailerons are verified to operate normally.
d. Repairs are made within 3 calendar days.
27-11-03-01.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the inoperative aileron PCU in the bypass mode, verify blocking mode operates normally and verify ailerons operate normally (AMM 27-00-00/901). NOTE: Do not do an Actuator Confidence Test, or an ACE Monitor Test, or L or R Aileron Actuator Confidence Tests.
27-11-03-01.operationsNote: When airspeed exceeds approximately 250 KIAS, air loads may cause the associated aileron to move slightly to a trailing-edge-up position while the opposite aileron will normally be commanded to a slight trailing-edge-down position. Some trim input may be necessary to correct for the resulting roll.

27-11-04-01.title: Flaperon Power Control Units (PCUs)............................................2.27-11-04.1 - Passenger
27-11-04-01.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative PCU is deactivated in the bypass mode.
b. Flaperons are verified to operate normally.
c. Repairs are made within 3 calendar days.
27-11-04-01.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the inoperative flaperon PCU in the bypass mode and verify flaperons operate normally (AMM 27-00-00/901). NOTE 1: Do not do an Actuator Confidence Test, or an ACE Monitor Test, or L or R Flaperon Actuator Confidence Tests. NOTE 2: The ACTUATOR PRESS SNSR status message will be displayed. The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 27-02-05.
27-11-04-01.operationsNote:
NOTE: For an inoperative right flaperon inboard PCU, the airplane must also
be dispatched using MMEL item 27-02-05.

For an inoperative right flaperon inboard PCU, the ACTUATOR PRESS SNSR status message will be displayed.

27-21-02.remarks: May be inoperative provided rudder trim is verified centered before each departure.
27-21-02.operationsNote:
Before each departure, verify rudder trim is centered.
1. Push the rudder trim Manual Trim Cancel switch or rotate Rudder Trim selector as required to center the rudder pedals.
2. Verify the rudder is centered by confirming the left and right rudder pedals are evenly aligned or the Flight Control Synoptic display RUDDER TRIM indication is zero (within
0.2 units left or right).

27-41-02.title: Alternate Pitch Trim Position Switches
27-41-02.remarks: One may be inoperative provided both control wheel pitch trim switches operate normally.

27-48-01.title: STAB Position Indicators
27-48-01.remarks: One may be inoperative provided it is blanked or covered.
27-48-01.operationsNote:
1. For a blank inoperative indicator, no action is required.
2. For an illuminated inoperative indicator, cover with tape or other material.

27-48-03.title: Nose Gear Pressure Switch (B-HNE-B-HNK)
27-48-03.remarks: May be inoperative provided stabilizer trim position is verified to be properly set before each departure.
27-48-03.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
For a Nose Gear Pressure switch leaking pneumatically, isolate the switch
(AMM 27-00-00/901).

Verify the stabilizer trim position is correct for the takeoff thrust, takeoff flaps, gross weight and center of gravity before each departure. NOTE: The STAB GREENBAND advisory message may be displayed.
1. Confirm the FMC takeoff data has been correctly initialized (takeoff thrust, takeoff flaps, gross weight, center of gravity).
2. Confirm the stabilizer trim is properly set to the position computed for the takeoff thrust, takeoff flaps, gross weight and center of gravity.

27-48-04.title: Nose Gear Pressure Transducer (B-HNM-Onwards)
27-48-04.remarks: May be inoperative provided stabilizer trim position is verified to be properly set before each departure.
27-48-04.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
For Nose Gear Pressure Transducer leaking pneumatically, isolate the
transducer (AMM 27-00-00/901).

Verify the stabilizer trim position is correct for the takeoff thrust, takeoff flaps, gross weight and center of gravity before each departure. NOTE: The STAB GREENBAND advisory message may be displayed.
1. Confirm the FMC takeoff data has been correctly initialized (takeoff thrust, takeoff flaps, gross weight, center of gravity).
2. Confirm the stabilizer trim is properly set to the position computed for the takeoff thrust, takeoff flaps, gross weight and center of gravity.

27-51-01.title: Inboard Flap, Outboard Support Mechanism Springs (No. 3 & No. 6 Supports)
27-51-01.remarks:

27-61-02.remarks:

27-61-02.operationsNote: For spoiler 7 SARD inoperative, overwing door 3L must be considered inoperative. For spoiler 8 SARD inoperative, overwing door 3R must be considered inoperative. The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 52-11-01.

27-61-03-01.operationsNote:
NOTE: Dispatch relief does not apply for a fault condition that is reported to

27-62-01.title: Automatic Speedbrake Function
27-62-01.remarks:
a. Automatic speedbrake function is deactivated.
b. Landing gear truck tilt pressure is verified to be normal before each flight.
c. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
27-62-01.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the automatic speedbrake and verify truck tilt pressure is normal before each flight (AMM 27-00-00/901).
27-62-01.operationsNote:
1. Base landing performance on manual speedbrakes.
2. Extend speedbrakes manually for rejected takeoff and landing. A. For rejected takeoff: 1) Simultaneously close the thrust levers, disengage the autothrottles and apply maximum manual wheel brakes or verify operation of RTO autobrakes. 2) Manually raise SPEED BRAKE lever. 3) Apply the maximum amount of reverse thrust consistent with conditions. B. For landing, use the AUTO SPEEDBRAKE Non-Normal Checklist. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item. 2AB.TO2A8D 2Y8-FLOW Section 2 Table of Contents ATA 28

28-11-01-01.title: Sump Drain Valves..................................2.28-11-01.1 - Surge Tanks
28-11-01-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided there is no evidence of leakage.
28-11-01-01.maintenanceNote: Visually inspect exterior surface location of the inoperative sump drain valve to verify that there is no evidence of fuel leakage (AMM 28-00-00/901).

28-11-01-02.title: Sump Drain Valves..................................2.28-11-01.1 - Main and Center Tanks
28-11-01-02.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. There is no evidence of leakage.
b. Alternate procedures are used to prevent water accumulation in associated tank.
28-11-01-02.maintenanceNote: Verify that there is no evidence of leakage and use alternate procedures to prevent water accumulation in associated tank (AMM 28-00-00/901).

28-21-01-01A.title: Pressure Fueling System......................2.28-21-01.1 - Refuel Valve Closed
28-21-01-01A.remarks:
a. Inoperative refuel valve(s) is closed.
b. Alternate procedures are used for refueling.
28-21-01-01A.maintenanceNote:
1. For one refuel valve inoperative closed per tank, use normal refueling procedures (refueling time for the associated tank will be increased).
2. For more than one refuel valve inoperative closed per tank (AMM 28-00-00/901).

28-21-01-01B.title: Pressure Fueling System......................2.28-21-01.1 - Refuel Valve Open
28-21-01-01B.remarks:
One main tank refuel valve may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative refuel valve is open.
b. Fuel jettison system is considered inoperative.
c. Alternate procedures are used for refueling.
28-21-01-01B.maintenanceNote: Use alternate refueling procedures (AMM 28-00-00/901). COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT item.
28-21-01-01B.operationsNote:
NOTE 1: There are 6 refuel valves installed on the 777 airplane, 2 for the left
main tank, 2 for the center tank, and 2 for the right main tank.
However, item MEL/DDG item 28-21-01-01B for an inoperative open
refuel valve offers dispatch relief only for either the left or right main
tank refuel valves. Dispatch is not allowed with an inoperative open
center tank refuel valve. Dispatch relief for an inoperative center
tank refuel valve is only available per item 28-21-01-01A with the
center tank refuel valve inoperative closed.
NOTE 2: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 28-31-01.

28-21-01-02-01.title: Pressure Fueling System......................2.28-21-01.1 - Fuel Quantity Indicators
28-21-01-02-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided alternate procedures are used for refueling.
28-21-01-02-01.maintenanceNote: Refuel airplane using one of the procedures provided in (AMM 28-00-00/901).

28-21-01-02-02.title: Pressure Fueling System......................2.28-21-01.1 - Load Select System
28-21-01-02-02.remarks: May be inoperative provided alternate procedures are used for refueling. NOTE: Any function which operates normally may be used.
28-21-01-02-02.maintenanceNote: NOTE: The Load Select System includes the four Load Select Indicators, the Load Select Quantity Selector, the four Load Select Set Switches and the Total/Backup Display Tank Select Switch. Use alternate procedures for refueling (AMM 28-00-00/901).

28-21-01-02-03.title: Pressure Fueling System......................2.28-21-01.1 - Refuel Valve Lights
28-21-01-02-03.remarks:
a. Overfill function operates normally.
b. Associated refuel valve is verified closed after each refueling.
28-21-01-02-03.maintenanceNote: Verify the associated valve is closed after each refueling (AMM 28-00-00/901).

28-21-01-02-04.title: Pressure Fueling System......................2.28-21-01.1 - Overfill Function (Normal/Reset Switch, Light and Test)
28-21-01-02-04.remarks:
a. Refuel valve lights operate normally.
b. Verify refuel valves close when appropriate during refueling.
28-21-01-02-04.maintenanceNote: Verify refuel valves close when appropriate during refueling (AMM 28-00-00/901).

28-21-01-02-05.title: Pressure Fueling System......................2.28-21-01.1 - Defuel Valve Function (Switch and Open Light)
28-21-01-02-05.remarks: May be inoperative provided defuel valve is considered inoperative.
28-21-01-02-05.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 28-26-01.

28-21-01-02-06.title: Pressure Fueling System......................2.28-21-01.1 - Power Switch - BATT Position
28-21-01-02-06.operationsNote:

28-21-01-02-07.title: Pressure Fueling System......................2.28-21-01.1 - Test Functions (Indication and System)
28-21-01-02-07.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
The integrated refuel panel also accomplishes an indication test during initial
power up.

28-21-01-02-08.title: Pressure Fueling System......................2.28-21-01.1 - Refuel Valve Switches
28-21-01-02-08.remarks:
a. Load select system operates normally.
b. Overfill function operates normally.
28-21-01-02-08.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
If one or more refuel valve switch(es) are inoperative closed, refer to MEL item

28-21-03.title: Refuel Adapters
28-21-03.remarks: May be inoperative provided there are no fuel leaks.
28-21-03.maintenanceNote: Immediately after refuel operations, inspect the area around the associated refuel adapter and verify fuel leaks are not present (AMM 28-00-00/901). NOTE 1: Dispatch is not allowed for an inoperative poppet valve. A poppet valve is not operating normally if it leaks immediately after refueling. NOTE 2: This item is applicable to failures of the refuel/defuel handle, break- away flange, or a break-away flange that is beyond wear limits. NOTE 3: An inoperative adapter should not be used in refuel or defuel operations.

28-22-01.title: Main Tank Fuel Pumps
28-22-01.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative main tank fuel pump is deactivated.
b. Both main tank quantity indications operate normally.
c. Flight remains within 120 minutes of landing at a suitable airport.

28-22-01-01.title: Main Tank Fuel Pumps..........................2.28-22-01.1 - PUMPS Switch PRESS Lights

28-22-01-02.title: Main Tank Fuel Pumps..........................2.28-22-01.1 - PUMPS Switch ON Lights

28-22-02A.title: Center Tank Fuel Override/Jettison Pumps......................2.28-22-02.1 - One Pump Inoperative
28-22-02A.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative pump is deactivated.
b. Center tank quantity indication operates normally.
c. With center tank fueled, fuel quantity remaining in main wing tanks is adequate to reach a suitable airport if remaining center pump fails at any time.
d. Center tank fuel is accounted for in the airplane weight and balance in the event center tank fuel cannot be used.
28-22-02A.operationsNote: 1. For center tank fuel: A. For center tank fuel required, ensure suitable airports can be reached with fuel in the main wing tanks in the event remaining center tank pump fails. B. Reduce the maximum zero fuel weight limit by the amount of center tank fuel. C. Adjust the zero fuel weight center of gravity forward limit based on the amount of center tank fuel. D. When operative center tank pump switch is ON, set one crossfeed switch open. E. When operative center tank pump switch is OFF, set crossfeed switches closed.

28-22-02B.title: Center Tank Fuel Override/Jettison Pumps......................2.28-22-02.1 - Both Pumps Inoperative
28-22-02B.remarks:
a. Pumps are deactivated.
b. Center tank quantity indication operates normally.
c. Center tank fuel is considered unusable and is accounted for in the airplane weight and balance. NOTE: AFM fuel loading and usage limitations are for usable fuel.
28-22-02B.operationsNote: 1. For center tank fuel: NOTE 1: Center tank fuel is considered unusable. FMC fuel prediction for INSUFFICIENT FUEL message on CDU will not be accurate. NOTE 2: FUEL IN CENTER advisory message may be displayed. A. Reduce the maximum zero fuel weight limit by the amount of center tank fuel. B. Adjust the zero fuel weight center of gravity forward limit based on the amount of center tank fuel.

28-22-02-01.title: Center Tank Fuel Override/Jettison Pumps......................2.28-22-02.1 - PUMPS Switch PRESS Lights

28-22-02-02.title: Center Tank Fuel Override/Jettison Pumps......................2.28-22-02.1 - PUMPS Switch ON Lights

28-22-03.title: Fuel Crossfeed Valves
28-22-03.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative fuel crossfeed valve is deactivated closed.
b. Remaining valve is verified to operate normally before each departure.
28-22-03.maintenanceNote: NOTE: The fuel imbalance pointer may appear if the affected crossfeed valve is in the open position when deactivated. Deactivate the affected crossfeed valve in the closed position (AMM 28-00-00/901).
28-22-03.operationsNote:
NOTE 1: The fuel imbalance pointer may appear. NOTE 2: The associated FUEL CROSSFEED AFT or FWD advisory message may be displayed for the crossfeed valve deactivated in the closed position. After the fuel pumps are ON, the fuel synoptic may incorrectly display a green flow line for the associated crossfeed valve. The EICAS display may have expanded fuel indications. NOTE 3: Before engine start, if the APU is used, the FUEL PRESS ENG L caution message and the FUEL PUMP R AFT and FUEL PUMP R FWD advisory messages may be displayed. Before each departure, perform the following fuel crossfeed valve check: (Required by AD 2019-19-10)
1. Position operative crossfeed valve on and verify associated FUEL CROSSFEED AFT or FWD advisory message does not display.
2. Position operative crossfeed valve off and verify associated FUEL CROSSFEED AFT or FWD advisory message does not display.

28-22-03-01.title: Fuel Crossfeed Valves...........................2.28-22-03.1 - CROSSFEED Switch VALVE Lights

28-22-04.title: Fuel Scavenge Systems
28-22-04.remarks:
a. Center tank quantity indication operates normally.
b. Appropriate amount of center tank fuel is considered unusable and is accounted for in the airplane weight and balance. NOTE: AFM fuel loading and usage limitations are for usable fuel.
28-22-04.operationsNote:
NOTE 1: For airplanes WITHOUT a modified CWT Scavenge System (HNE-
HNK, HNS-HNX):
The fuel scavenge system includes the jet pump and two shutoff
valves in each system. If the jet pump is inoperative or either shutoff
valve is inoperative closed, the associated system is inoperative. For
more than one system shutoff valve inoperative open, use MEL item
28-22-06B.
NOTE 2: For airplanes WITH a modified CWT Scavenge System (HNM-HNQ,
HNR, KPA-KQZ) :
The main tank fuel jettison system’s pumps provide the motive
power to the fuel scavenge system’s jet pumps, and the shutoff
valves are not installed. If a jet pump is inoperative, or if the
