29-11-02.title: Center System Primary Alternating Current Motor Pumps (ACMP)
29-11-02.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative center ACMP is deactivated.
b. Both center ADPs operate normally.
29-11-02.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the inoperative center system primary pump (AMM 29-00-00/901).
29-11-02.operationsNote:
1. For center system PRIMARY C1 ELEC pump inoperative, position PRIMARY C1 ELEC switch off.
2. For center system PRIMARY C2 ELEC pump inoperative, position PRIMARY C2 ELEC switch off.
3. Due to reduced center hydraulic system power, EICAS messages may appear on ground due to operation of systems powered by this system. Operation of the following functions will impact the center hydraulic system: Nose Gear Steering, Main Gear Steering, Flaps, Slats, Flight Controls and Stabilizer. Steering inputs greater than 13 degrees by tiller input or towing may result in display of main gear related messages. The AUTO SPEEDBRAKE advisory message may display and latch on the ground.
4. To avoid display of EICAS messages related to low center system hydraulic pressure while on the ground, position one center system DEMAND pump (ADP) selector ON while conducting ground operations.

29-11-03A.title: HYD PUMP DEM C1 or C2 - ADP Verified Not Running
29-11-03A.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative ADP is selected off.
b. Both center system ACMPs operate normally.
c. Remaining ADP heater operates normally.
d. Remaining ADP AUTO function operates normally.
e. Associated pump is verified not running when selected OFF.
f. APU is used as ADP air source during takeoff.
g. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
29-11-03A.maintenanceNote: Verify the inoperative center system demand ADP is not running when selected OFF and the remaining center system demand ADP heater operates normally (AMM 29-00-00/901).
29-11-03A.operationsNote:
NOTE: For APU-to-Pack takeoff function installed (300ER), the APU-to-Pack Takeoff Supplementary Procedure is not allowed.
1. Reduce the performance limited weights by the appropriate adjustments. Performance Limited Takeoff Climb Takeoff Runway/Obstacle Weights -300ER 771 kg 4,355 kg -300 181 kg 1,678 kg
2. Position the inoperative center system DEMAND pump selector OFF.
3. For takeoff, configure the pneumatic system with the APU supplying air for the remaining operative center system demand pump. A. Position APU Bleed air switch AUTO. B. Start the APU if it is not operating. C. Position Bleed Isolation L ISLN and R ISLN switches CLOSED. NOTE: The BLEED ISLN CLOSED L and BLEED ISLN CLOSED R advisory messages will be displayed. D. After takeoff is completed, position Bleed Isolation L ISLN and R ISLN switches AUTO and configure the APU as required. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

29-11-03B.title: HYD PUMP DEM C1 or C2 - ADP Deactivated
29-11-03B.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative ADP is deactivated.
b. Both center system ACMPs operate normally.
c. Remaining ADP heater operates normally.
d. Remaining ADP AUTO function operates normally.
e. APU is used as ADP air source during takeoff.
f. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
29-11-03B.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the inoperative ADP and verify the remaining center system demand ADP heater operates normally (AMM 29-00-00/901).
29-11-03B.operationsNote:
NOTE: For APU-to-Pack takeoff function installed, the APU-to-Pack Takeoff Supplementary Procedure is not allowed.
1. Reduce the performance limited weights by the appropriate adjustments. Performance Limited Takeoff Climb Takeoff Runway/Obstacle Weights -300ER 771 kg 4,355 kg -300 181 kg 1,678 kg
2. Position the inoperative center system DEMAND pump selector OFF.
3. For takeoff, configure the pneumatic system with the APU supplying air for the remaining operative center system demand pump. A. Position APU Bleed air switch AUTO. B. Start the APU if it is not operating. C. Position Bleed Isolation L ISLN and R ISLN switches CLOSED. NOTE: The BLEED ISLN CLOSED L and BLEED ISLN CLOSED R advisory messages will be displayed. D. After takeoff is completed, position Bleed Isolation L ISLN and R ISLN switches AUTO and configure the APU as required. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

29-11-03C.title: HYD PUMP DEM C1 or C2 - Other ADP Auto/Heater Function Inoperative
29-11-03C.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative ADP is selected off.
b. Both center system ACMPs operate normally.
c. Associated pump is verified not running when selected OFF.
d. Remaining ADP is selected ON for the entire flight.
e. APU is used as ADP air source during takeoff.
f. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
29-11-03C.maintenanceNote: Verify the inoperative center system demand ADP is not running when selected OFF. If required, disconnect the ADP so it does not run (AMM 29-00-00/901).
29-11-03C.operationsNote:
NOTE: For APU-to-Pack takeoff function installed (300ER), the APU-to-Pack Takeoff Supplementary Procedure is not allowed.
1. Reduce the performance limited weights by the appropriate adjustments. Performance Limited Takeoff Climb Takeoff Runway/Obstacle Weights -300ER 771 kg 4,355 kg -300 181 kg 1,678 kg
2. Position the inoperative center system DEMAND pump selector OFF.
3. Position remaining operative center system DEMAND pump selector ON prior to takeoff and leave ON for the entire flight. NOTE: Do not position center system DEMAND pump selector ON before engine start.
4. For takeoff, configure the pneumatic system with the APU supplying air for the remaining operative center system demand pump. A. Position APU Bleed air switch AUTO. B. Start the APU if it is not operating. C. Position Bleed Isolation L ISLN and R ISLN switches CLOSED. NOTE: The BLEED ISLN CLOSED L and BLEED ISLN CLOSED R advisory messages will be displayed. D. After takeoff is completed, position Bleed Isolation L ISLN and R ISLN switches AUTO and configure the APU as required. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

29-11-03-01A.title: HYD PUMP DEM C1 or C2 - Other ADP Operates Normally
29-11-03-01A.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Remaining ADP operates normally.
b. Associated ADP ON and OFF selector positions are verified to operate normally.
c. Associated ADP is selected ON for the entire flight.
29-11-03-01A.maintenanceNote: Verify the associated center system demand ADP selector ON and OFF positions operate normally (AMM 29-00-00/901).
29-11-03-01A.operationsNote:
1. Position associated center system DEMAND pump selector ON prior to takeoff and leave ON for the entire flight. NOTE: Do not position center system DEMAND pump selector ON before engine start.
2. Position remaining center system DEMAND pump selector AUTO.

29-11-03-01B.title: HYD PUMP DEM C1 or C2 - Other ADP Inoperative
29-11-03-01B.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Both center system ACMPs operate normally.
b. Associated ADP ON and OFF selector positions are verified to operate normally.
c. Associated ADP is selected ON for the entire flight.
d. APU is used as ADP air source during takeoff.
e. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
29-11-03-01B.maintenanceNote: Verify the associated center system demand ADP selector ON and OFF positions operate normally (AMM 29-00-00/901).
29-11-03-01B.operationsNote:
NOTE: For APU-to-Pack takeoff function installed (300ER), the APU-to-Pack Takeoff Supplementary Procedure is not allowed. Reduce the performance limited weights by the appropriate adjustments. NOTE: For airplane also dispatched using MEL item 29-11-03C, it is not required to add the following penalties. Performance Limited Takeoff Climb Takeoff Runway/Obstacle Weights -300ER 771 kg 4,355 kg -300 181 kg 1,678 kg
1. Position inoperative center system DEMAND pump selector OFF.
2. Position associated center system DEMAND pump selector ON prior to takeoff and leave ON for the entire flight. NOTE: Do not position center system DEMAND pump selector ON before engine start.
3. For takeoff, configure the pneumatic system with the APU supplying air for the operating center system demand pump. A. Position APU Bleed air switch AUTO. B. Start the APU if it is not operating. C. Position Bleed Isolation L ISLN and R ISLN switches CLOSED. NOTE: The BLEED ISLN CLOSED L and BLEED ISLN CLOSED R advisory messages will be displayed. D. After takeoff is completed, position Bleed Isolation L ISLN and R ISLN switches AUTO and configure the APU as required. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE
1. This is an OPT MEL item.
2. For Center System Demand Air Driven Pumps there is no requirement to reconfigure Bleed ISLN to take-off configuration for approach and landing as the APU air source is only required for take-off to ensure full rudder authority in the event of a low speed engine failure.

29-11-03-01C.title: HYD PUMP DEM C1 or C2 - Both Auto/Heater Functions Inoperative
29-11-03-01C.remarks:
a. Both center system ACMPs operate normally.
b. ADP ON and OFF selector positions are verified to operate normally for both pumps.
c. One ADP is selected ON for the entire flight.
d. APU is used as ADP air source during takeoff.
e. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
29-11-03-01C.maintenanceNote: Verify both center system demand ADP selector’s ON and OFF positions operate normally (AMM 29-00-00/901).
29-11-03-01C.operationsNote:
NOTE: For APU-to-Pack takeoff function installed (300ER), the APU-to-Pack Takeoff Supplementary Procedure is not allowed.
1. Reduce the performance limited weights by the appropriate adjustments. Performance Limited Takeoff Climb Takeoff Runway/Obstacle Weights -300ER 771 kg 4,355 kg -300 181 kg 1,678 kg
2. Position one center system DEMAND pump selector ON prior to takeoff and leave ON for the entire flight. NOTE: Do not position center system DEMAND pump selector ON before engine start.
3. Position remaining center system DEMAND pump selector AUTO.
4. For takeoff, configure the pneumatic system with the APU supplying air for the operating center system demand pump. A. Position APU Bleed air switch AUTO. B. Start the APU if it is not operating. C. Position Bleed Isolation L ISLN and R ISLN switches CLOSED. NOTE: The BLEED ISLN CLOSED L and BLEED ISLN CLOSED R advisory messages will be displayed. D. After takeoff is completed, position Bleed Isolation L ISLN and R ISLN switches AUTO and configure the APU as required. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE
1. This is an OPT MEL item.
2. For Center System Demand Air Driven Pumps there is no requirement to reconfigure Bleed ISLN to take-off configuration for approach and landing as the APU air source is only required for take-off to ensure full rudder authority in the event of a low speed engine failure.

29-11-04-01.title: Demand Pump Selectors........................2.29-11-04.1 - Center System AUTO Position
29-11-04-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided associated demand ADP auto function is considered inoperative.
29-11-04-01.operationsNote: NOTE: The airplane must be dispatched using MEL item 29-11-03-01.

29-11-04-02.title: Demand Pump Selectors........................2.29-11-04.1 - Left & Right System AUTO Position
29-11-04-02.remarks:
a. ON and OFF positions operate normally.
b. Associated pump selector is ON for takeoff and landing.
29-11-04-02.operationsNote: Position the associated DEMAND pump selector ON for takeoff and landing. NOTE: Selector may be placed in ON position for the entire flight if desired.

29-11-04-03.title: Demand Pump Selectors........................2.29-11-04.1 - ON Position
29-11-04-03.remarks: May be inoperative provided the AUTO and OFF positions for associated pump operate normally.

29-11-05.title: Hydraulic Interface Module (HYDIM) Cards
29-11-05.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative card is in the HYDIM center right (HCR) card position.
b. Individual center system pump pressure indications operate normally.
c. Center system demand ADP C1 auto function is considered inoperative.
29-11-05.maintenanceNote: Inoperative HYDIM card must be in the HYDIM Center Right (CR) card position. Configure HYDIM cards as required (AMM 29-00-00/901).
29-11-05.operationsNote:
NOTE: The airplane must be dispatched using MEL item 29-11-03-01 for one
inoperative.

The Hydraulic Synoptic Display may have incomplete or missing information.

29-11-06.title: Center Hydraulic Isolation System
29-11-06.remarks: May be inoperative provided center hydraulic isolation system is deactivated open.
29-11-06.maintenanceNote: Deactivate center hydraulic isolation system with the reserve and nose gear isolation valves in the open position (AMM 29-00-00/901).
29-11-06.operationsNote: The RESERVE BRAKES/STRG advisory message will be displayed. Do not accomplish the RESERVE BRAKES/STRG Non-Normal Checklist. For failures resulting in HYD PRESS SYS C caution message being displayed, accomplish the HYD PRESS SYS C and the RESERVE BRAKES/STRG Non- Normal Checklists.

29-21-01.title: RAT Heater System 29-21-01-01 -300/-300ER
29-21-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided repairs are made within 3 calendar days.
29-21-01.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
The RAT heater system is considered to be operating normally when the heater
switch (E6 bay) is moved from its existing position to the other position
(HEATER 1 or HEATER 2) and the RAT GEN HEAT status message clears
when the RAT heater is tested (AMM 29-21-00/501).

29-30-01-01.title: Hydraulic Pump Lights..........................2.29-30-01.1 - FAULT Lights
29-30-01-01.remarks: One in each system may be inoperative.

29-30-02.title: Hydraulic Synoptic Display
29-30-02.operationsNote: For missing data on the Synoptic Display, selecting an alternate location for the display (L INBD, LWR CTR, or R INBD) may restore the missing data. Synoptic Displays containing missing data may continue to be used to the extent remaining data is useful. Airplane system faults will be annunciated by alerting and status messages.

29-31-01.title: Hydraulic System Pressure Transducers
29-31-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided all associated system pump pressure indications operate normally.

29-31-02-01.title: Pump Pressure Indication Systems..................................................2.29-31-02.1 - Left & Right Systems
29-31-02-01.remarks:
One in each system may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated system pressure transducer operates normally.
b. Associated pump operation is verified normal before each departure.
29-31-02-01.maintenanceNote: Verify the associated pump is operating normally before each departure. For pump status message displayed, verify the associated pump pressure indication transducer is the malfunction and disconnect that transducer (AMM 29-00-00/901).
29-31-02-01.operationsNote:
NOTE: The pump transducer may fail such that the associated pump status
message is displayed rather than the pump pressure indication status
message.

For a pump pressure transducer disconnected, the associated pump pressure advisory message will be displayed and the hydraulic synoptic flow bars may not indicate correctly.

29-31-02-02A.title: Pump Pressure Indication Systems..................................................2.29-31-02.1 - Pump Operative
29-31-02-02A.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated system pressure transducer operates normally.
b. Associated pump operation is verified normal before each departure.
29-31-02-02A.maintenanceNote: Verify the associated pump is operating normally before each departure (AMM 29-00-00/901).

29-31-02-02B.title: Pump Pressure Indication Systems..................................................2.29-31-02.1 - Pump Inoperative
29-31-02-02B.remarks: One may be inoperative for an associated inoperative pump.

29-32-01-01.title: Pump Temperature Indications..............................................2.29-32-01.1 - Left & Right Systems
29-32-01-01.remarks:
One in each system may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated pump pressure indications operate normally.
b. Associated pump operation is verified normal before each departure.
29-32-01-01.maintenanceNote: Verify the associated pump is operating normally by verifying the pump pressure is normal before each departure (AMM 29-00-00/901).

29-32-01-02A.title: Pump Temperature Indications..............................................2.29-32-01.1 - Pump Operative
29-32-01-02A.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated pump pressure indications operate normally.
b. Associated pump operation is verified normal before each departure.
29-32-01-02A.maintenanceNote: Verify the associated pump is operating normally by verifying the pump pressure is normal before each departure (AMM 29-00-00/901).

29-32-01-02B.title: Pump Temperature Indications..............................................2.29-32-01.1 - Pump Inoperative
29-32-01-02B.remarks: One may be inoperative for an associated inoperative pump.

29-33-01.title: Hydraulic Fluid Quantity Indications (Flight Deck)
29-33-01.remarks:
Two may be inoperative provided:
a. Reservoir level is verified normal before each departure.
b. Associated system pressure indication operates normally.
c. For the center system indication inoperative, center hydraulic isolation system is considered inoperative.
29-33-01.maintenanceNote: Verify the associated system reservoir quantity level is normal before each departure, and for center quantity indication inoperative, deactivate Center Hydraulic Isolation System (AMM 29-00-00/901). 2AB.TO3A0D 3Y0-FLOW Section 2 Table of Contents ATA 30
29-33-01.operationsNote:
NOTE: For the center system indication inoperative, the airplane must also be
dispatched using MEL item 29-11-06.

30-11-01.title: Wing Anti-Ice Systems
30-11-01.remarks:
a. Associated valve is locked closed.
b. Wing anti-ice control switch remains OFF.
c. Airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions.
30-11-01.maintenanceNote: Lock the associated Wing Anti-Ice (WAI) valve(s) in the closed position (AMM 30-00-00/901). COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

30-11-02.title: Wing Anti-Ice Control (Card and Switch)
30-11-02.remarks:
a. Both wing anti-ice valves are locked closed.
b. Wing anti-ice control switch remains OFF.
c. Airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions.
30-11-02.maintenanceNote: Lock both Wing Anti-Ice (WAI) valves in the closed position (AMM 30-00-00/901). COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

30-21-01.title: Engine Anti-Ice Systems
30-21-01.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Valve is locked closed.
b. Associated engine anti-ice control switch remains OFF.
c. Airplane is not operated in known or forecast icing conditions.
d. Flight remains within 120 minutes of landing at a suitable airport.
30-21-01.maintenanceNote: Lock associated EAI valve in the closed position (AMM 30-00-00/901).
30-21-01.companyMaintenanceNote: In order to protect subsequent flights that may be subject to known or forecast icing conditions, it is preferable to apply item 30-21-01-01A, -01B, -01C, -01D. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

30-21-01-01A.title: Engine Anti-Ice Systems.......................2.30-21-01.1 - OAT 38 Degrees C or Below, With Deactivation Kit Installed
30-21-01-01A.remarks:
For operations at ambient temperature 38 degrees C or below, one may be inoperative provided:
a. Valve is deactivated open using deactivation kit.
b. Engine fan case overheat detection system operates normally.
c. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
30-21-01-01A.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the associated EAI valve by installing the EAI valve lock-open kit, P/N K28703 (AMM 30-00-00/901). NOTE: Dispatch is not allowed with EAI LOOPS FANCASE L or R status message displayed.
30-21-01-01A.operationsNote:
NOTE: Dispatch is not allowed with EAI LOOPS FANCASE L or R status message displayed.
1. Reduce performance limited weights by the appropriate adjustments. Performance Limited Weights Takeoff & Landing Enroute Climb -300 9,979 kg 10,659 kg NOTE: The enroute climb weight penalties listed above are based on single engine operating speeds that approximate maximum lift- to-drag ratio speed. To account for the difference in level off altitude when operating at other speeds, multiply the enroute climb weight penalty listed above by the appropriate factor listed on page
3.00-01-00.2 in the ENROUTE DIVERSION SPEED EFFECTS paragraph.
2. Increase flight planning fuel by
0.5% for an inoperative EAI Valve or EAI Pressure Sensor, or by
0.8% for an inoperative EAI Card.
3. For EDTO flight planning increase the EDTO engine inoperative Critical Fuel Reserves by
0.9%.
4. Position ENGINE ANTI-ICE selector(s) as follows: A. For EAI Valve or EAI Pressure Sensor inoperative, position associated EAI selector ON. NOTE 1: When an EAI selector is positioned to ON and the temperature is greater than 10 degrees C, the ANTI-ICE ON advisory message will be displayed. Do not accomplish the ANTI-ICE ON Non-Normal Checklist. NOTE 2: Inflight, the ENG IDLE DISAGREE advisory message may be displayed when engine thrust is reduced to idle. B. For EAI Card inoperative, position both EAI selectors ON. NOTE 1: When an EAI selector is positioned to ON and the temperature is greater than 10 degrees C, the ANTI-ICE ON advisory message will be displayed. Do not accomplish the ANTI-ICE ON Non-Normal Checklist. NOTE 2: The associated ANTI-ICE ENG L or R advisory message will be displayed, the EAI indication will not be displayed on EICAS, and the associated EAI valve will be displayed as invalid (low intensity white) and the green flow bar will not be displayed on the Air synoptic.
5. For the inoperative EAI valve, if the ANTI-ICE LEAK ENG L or R caution message is subsequently displayed: Do not accomplish the initial one minute delay associated with the ANTI-ICE LEAK ENG L or R Non-Normal Checklist. Complete the remainder of the checklist as soon as practical. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

30-21-01-01B.title: Engine Anti-Ice Systems.......................2.30-21-01.1 - OAT 38 Degrees C or Below, Without Deactivation Kit Installed
30-21-01-01B.remarks:
For operations at ambient temperature 38 degrees C or below, one may be inoperative provided:
a. Valve is electrically disconnected and verified open.
b. Engine fan case overheat detection system operates normally.
c. Associated EAI pressure sensor system operates normally.
d. Associated EAI card operates normally.
e. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
30-21-01-01B.maintenanceNote: For EAI VALVE L or R status message displayed, deactivate the EAI valve by disconnecting the electrical connector and verify EAI valve is open when the associated engine is running (AMM 30-00-00/901). NOTE: Dispatch is not allowed with EAI LOOPS FANCASE L or R status message displayed.
30-21-01-01B.operationsNote:
NOTE: Dispatch is not allowed with EAI LOOPS FANCASE L or R status message displayed.
1. Reduce performance limited weights by the appropriate adjustments. NOTE: The enroute climb weight penalties listed above are based on single engine operating speeds that approximate maximum lift- to-drag ratio speed. To account for the difference in level off altitude when operating at other speeds, multiply the enroute climb weight penalty listed above by the appropriate factor listed on page
3.00-01-00.2 in the ENROUTE DIVERSION SPEED EFFECTS paragraph. Performance Limited Weights Takeoff & Landing Enroute Climb -300 9,979 kg 10,659 kg
2. Increase flight planning fuel by
0.5%.
3. For EDTO flight planning Increase the EDTO engine inoperative Critical Fuel Reserves by
0.9%.
4. Verify the EAI valve is open when the associated engine is running before each departure. A. Position associated ANTI-ICE Panel (P5) Engine Anti-Ice selector OFF. B. After the associated engine has been started, confirm the associated EAI indication (green EAI) is displayed above the N1 indication. NOTE 1: If the EAI indication is not displayed, the valve may be stuck closed and a thrust setting slightly above minimum idle may open the valve. NOTE 2: On the Air synoptic, the EAI valve will indicate failed open because the EAI selector is OFF and the green flow bar will be displayed.
5. Position associated ENGINE ANTI-ICE selector ON. NOTE 1: When an EAI selector is positioned to ON and the temperature is greater than 10 degrees C, the ANTI-ICE ON advisory message will be displayed. Do not accomplish the ANTI-ICE ON Non-Normal Checklist. NOTE 2: Inflight, the ENG IDLE DISAGREE advisory message may be displayed when engine thrust is reduced to idle. NOTE 3: The ANTI-ICE ENG advisory message may be displayed during ground operations prior to takeoff. Flight crew should accomplish the associated non-normal checklist. If ANTI-ICE ENG clears, takeoff is allowed.
6. For the inoperative EAI valve, if the ANTI-ICE LEAK ENG L or R caution message is subsequently displayed: Do not accomplish the initial one minute delay associated with the ANTI- ICE LEAK ENG L or R Non-Normal Checklist. Complete the remainder of the checklist as soon as practical. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

30-21-01-01C.title: Engine Anti-Ice Systems.......................2.30-21-01.1 - OAT Above 38 Degrees C, With Deactivation Kit Installed
30-21-01-01C.remarks:
For operations at ambient temperature above 38 degrees C, one may be inoperative provided:
a. Valve is deactivated open using deactivation kit.
b. Engine fan case overheat detection system operates normally.
c. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
d. Repairs are made within 3 calendar days.
30-21-01-01C.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the associated EAI valve by installing the EAI valve lock-open kit, P/N K28703 (AMM 30-00-00/901). NOTE: Dispatch is not allowed with EAI LOOPS FANCASE L or R status message displayed.
30-21-01-01C.operationsNote:
NOTE: Dispatch is not allowed with EAI LOOPS FANCASE L or R status message displayed.
1. Reduce performance limited weights by the appropriate adjustments. Performance Limited Weights Takeoff & Landing Enroute Climb -300 9,979 kg 10,659 kg NOTE: The enroute climb weight penalties listed above are based on single engine operating speeds that approximate maximum lift- to-drag ratio speed. To account for the difference in level off altitude when operating at other speeds, multiply the enroute climb weight penalty listed above by the appropriate factor listed on page
3.00-01-00.2 in the ENROUTE DIVERSION SPEED EFFECTS paragraph.
2. Increase flight planning fuel by
0.5%.
3. For EDTO flight planning Increase the EDTO engine inoperative Critical Fuel Reserves by
0.9%.
4. Verify the EAI valve is open when the associated engine is running before each departure. A. Position associated ANTI-ICE Panel (P5) Engine Anti-Ice selector OFF. B. After the associated engine has been started, confirm the associated EAI indication (green EAI) is displayed above the N1 indication. NOTE 1: If the EAI indication is not displayed, the valve may be stuck closed and a thrust setting slightly above minimum idle may open the valve. NOTE 2: On the Air synoptic, the EAI valve will indicate failed open because the EAI selector is OFF and the green flow bar will be displayed.
5. Position associated ENGINE ANTI-ICE selector ON. NOTE 1: When an EAI selector is positioned to ON and the temperature is greater than 10 degrees C, the ANTI-ICE ON advisory message will be displayed. Do not accomplish the ANTI-ICE ON Non-Normal Checklist. NOTE 2: Inflight, the ENG IDLE DISAGREE advisory message may be displayed when engine thrust is reduced to idle.
6. For the inoperative EAI valve, if the ANTI-ICE LEAK ENG L or R caution message is subsequently displayed: A. Do not accomplish the initial one minute delay associated with the ANTI-ICE LEAK ENG L or R Non-Normal Checklist. Complete the remainder of the checklist as soon as practical. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

30-21-01-01D.title: Engine Anti-Ice Systems.......................2.30-21-01.1 - OAT Above 38 Degrees C, Without Deactivation Kit Installed
30-21-01-01D.remarks:
For operations at ambient temperature above 38 degrees C, one may be inoperative provided:

b. Engine fan case overheat detection system operates normally.
c. Associated EAI pressure sensor system operates normally.
d. Associated EAI card operates normally.

f. Repairs are made within 3 calendar days.
30-21-01-01D.maintenanceNote: For EAI VALVE L or R status message displayed, deactivate the EAI valve by disconnecting the electrical connector and verify EAI valve is open when the associated engine is running (AMM 30-00-00/901). NOTE: Dispatch is not allowed with EAI LOOPS FANCASE L or R status message displayed.
30-21-01-01D.operationsNote:
NOTE: Dispatch is not allowed with EAI LOOPS FANCASE L or R status message displayed.
1. Reduce performance limited weights by the appropriate adjustments. Performance Limited Weights Takeoff & Landing Enroute Climb -300 9,979 kg 10,659 kg NOTE: The enroute climb weight penalties listed above are based on single engine operating speeds that approximate maximum lift- to-drag ratio speed. To account for the difference in level off altitude when operating at other speeds, multiply the enroute climb weight penalty listed above by the appropriate factor listed on page
3.00-01-00.2 in the ENROUTE DIVERSION SPEED EFFECTS paragraph.
2. Increase flight planning fuel by
0.5%.
3. For EDTO flight planning Increase the EDTO engine inoperative Critical Fuel Reserves by

e. Standby airspeed indication operates normally.
f. Right AIR DATA/ATT instrument source switch operates normally.
g. Approach minimums do not require its use.
h. SAARU data is verified to be available to the right PFD before each departure.
i. Left and center pitot probes are inspected before each departure.
30-31-01-01.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the right Pitot Air Data Module (ADM), inspect the left and center Pitot Probes before each departure, and verify SAARU data is available to the right Primary Flight Display (PFD) before each departure (AMM 30-00-00/901). NOTE 1: The PITOT ADM R status message will be displayed. NOTE 2: The AOA VANE R status message will be displayed. For Collins weather radar installed (B-HNS - B-HNX) NOTE 3: AUTOTILT FAIL will be annunciated on the ND.Gain access to the Right Flight Controls Power Supply Assembly (PSA) on Equipment Rack E5-1. NOTE 4: The left, center and right Pitot and Static ADMs are interchangeable.
30-31-01-01.operationsNote:
NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL items
34-21-04-01, 34-21-06 and 22-11-07-01.

1. The autoland system is not fail-operational and the NO LAND 3 advisory message will be displayed.
2. If the Captain’s AIR DATA/ATT instrument source switch is positioned to ALTN, airspeed will be flagged on the left PFD. This effect is normal for this dispatch condition.
3. An additional failure, such as a plugged or damaged pitot probe, may result in the two remaining pitot sources miscomparing and voted airspeed being declared invalid (if the center Pitot Heat is inoperative, data from the center Pitot ADM is not used in the voted airspeed determination). Lack of valid voted airspeed will result in display of the NAV AIR DATA SYS advisory or AIR DATA SYS Caution message and single channel airspeed and altitude will be displayed on the PFDs. NOTE: For a right PFD airspeed flagged, selection of the First Officer’s AIR DATA/ATT switch to ALTN will display the left PFD airspeed on the right PFD. This single airspeed condition will be indicated by the SGL SOURCE AIR DATA advisory message. The following display effects with regard to airspeed (A/S) are possible: Pitot Heat Pitot Probe Standby A/S R PFD A/S L PFD A/S Inop/Pitot Plugged, Display Display Display ADM Deact. Damaged, etc. At Dispatch Right Left In Error Correct Flag (plugged) (ADM deact.) Right Center Correct In Error Flag (plugged) (ADM deact.)

31-33-01.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
If desired, the Airborne Printer can be deactivated by opening and collaring the
P210 panel FLT DECK PRINTER circuit breaker.

31-35-01.title: Quick Access Recorder
31-35-01.operationsNote:
NOTE 1: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 23-15-01.
NOTE 2: For avWifi installed, the airplane must be dispatched using MEL item
46-30-01-01.
NOTE 3: The avRDC Max QAR that is installed on all aircraft provides the
interface for the satLINK MAX and the avWifi systems.

31-41-01-01.title: Airplane Information Management System (AIMS)......................................................2.31-41-03.1 - AIMS-2 Cabinet Bus
31-41-01-01.remarks: May be dispatched with AIMS CABINET BUS faults.
31-41-01-01.operationsNote:
NOTE: Cabin Wifi will be inoperative. The airplane must also be dispatched
using MEL item 44-20-00.

31-51-01.title: Master Warning Lights (Glareshield)
31-51-01.remarks: One may be inoperative provided the aural for the master warning system operates normally.

31-51-02.title: Master Caution Lights (Glareshield)
31-51-02.remarks: One may be inoperative provided the aural for the master caution system operates normally.

31-51-03.title: Aural Warning Speaker Systems
31-51-03.remarks: One may be inoperative provided master warning and master caution lights operate normally.

31-51-04-01A.title: Warning Electronics System (WES) Channels.......................2.31-51-04.1 - Channel Not Deactivated
31-51-04-01A.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Both stabilizer position indicators operate normally.
b. SPEED LIM flag is not displayed adjacent to the airspeed indication on either PFD.
31-51-04-01A.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
The stabilizer position indicator operates normally if the stabilizer position and
green band are displayed on the indicator (indicators not blanked).

31-51-04-01B.title: Warning Electronics System (WES) Channels.......................2.31-51-04.1 - Channel Deactivated
31-51-04-01B.remarks: One WES channel may be inoperative provided it is deactivated.
31-51-04-01B.maintenanceNote:
NOTE: The warning electronic system (WES) consists of four warning electronic unit (WEU) channels. Deactivate the inoperative WEU channel (AMM 31-00-00/901).
1. For WEU CHANNEL L1. NOTE: STALL WARNING SYS L and WARNING SPEAKER L status messages will be displayed. The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL items 27-32-01 and 31-51-03.
2. For WEU CHANNEL L2. NOTE: STALL WARNING SYS L status message will be displayed. The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 27-32-01.
3. For WEU CHANNEL R1. NOTE: STALL WARNING SYS R and WARNING SPEAKER R status messages will be displayed. The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL items 27-32-01 and 31-51-03.
4. For WEU CHANNEL R2. NOTE: STALL WARNING SYS R status message will be displayed. The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 27-32-01.

31-51-05.title: Warning Electronic System (WES) Autopilot Disconnect Warning Function
31-51-05.remarks:
a. Autopilots are not used.
b. Approach minimums do not require use of the autopilots.
c. Number of flight segments and segment duration is acceptable to flight crew.
d. Enroute operations do not require use of the autopilots.
e. Flight remains within 180 minutes of landing at a suitable airport.
31-51-05.operationsNote:
NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 22-11-07.

Do not use the autopilots and observe the following restrictions:
1. Approach minimums must not require autopilot use.
2. Enroute operations must not require autopilot use.
3. The flight must remain within 180 minutes of landing at a suitable airport.
4. For PBN operations: A. PBN operations using autopilot are not allowed. B. PBN operations may be conducted using flight director provided its use is appropriate for the intended operation. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE If the MEL item has been raised after the ATC Flight Plan has been received, contact Flight Dispatch to verify that the ATC Flight Plan reflects the current aircraft equipment capability based on the MEL item.

31-51-05-01.title: Warning Electronic System (WES) Autopilot Disconnect Warning Function..................................................2.31-51-05.1 - WES Autopilot Interfaces
31-51-05-01.remarks: One may be inoperative provided the WES autopilot disconnect warning function is verified to operate normally.
31-51-05-01.operationsNote:
Verify the Warning Electronic System (WES) autopilot disconnect warning function operates normally.
1. Engage, then manually disengage the autopilots.
2. Confirm illumination of the master warning lights, activation of an aural indication and display of the AUTOPILOT DISC warning message.

31-61-01.title: Display Units (DU)
31-61-01.remarks: One may be inoperative in the lower center DU position.
31-61-01.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
1. The six display units are interchangeable. If the inoperative display unit is
in a location other than the lower center position, it can be replaced with
the operative unit from the lower center position.
2. For a non-video capable display unit installed in the left or right inboard or
in the lower center display locations, ground maneuver camera video will
not be available on that display.
3. For a non-video capable display unit installed in the left or right inboard or
in the lower center display locations, Flight Deck Door Visual Surveillance
System video will not be available on that display.
4. Refer to AMM 31-61-01/401 for DU removal and installation procedures.

31-61-02B.title: Cursor Control Devices (CCD).......................................................2.31-61-02.1 - Both Inoperative
31-61-02B.remarks: May be inoperative provided alternate procedures are established and used.
31-61-02B.operationsNote:
Alternate procedures require that paper checklist procedures must be used. Data communications functions such as ACARS are not accessible on an MFD and require alternate procedures. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE
1. This item affects Performance Based Communications and Surveillance (PBCS) capability. (Refer to MEL Section 0 Presentation - Airspace Related Requirements)
2. If the MEL item has been raised after the ATC flight plan has been received, contact Flight Dispatch to verify that the ATC Flight Plan reflects the current aircraft capability based on the MEL item.

31-61-02-02.title: Cursor Control Devices (CCD).......................................................2.31-61-02.1 - Cursor Location Switch Lights

31-61-03.title: Remote Light Sensor (RLS) System
31-61-03.remarks: May be inoperative provided all manual display brightness controls operate normally.

31-61-04.title: Display Select Panel (DSP)
31-61-04.remarks:
a. The left and right CDU DSP backup features are verified to operate normally.
b. The ground maneuver camera system is considered inoperative.
c. The flight deck door visual surveillance system is considered inoperative.
31-61-04.maintenanceNote: Verify the left and right CDU DSP backup features operate normally (AMM 31-00-00/901).
31-61-04.operationsNote:
NOTE 1: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 31-61-10.
NOTE 2: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 23-70-01.

Use the CDU Display Select Panel (DSP) backup feature.

31-61-04-03.title: Display Select Panel (DSP).......................................................2.31-61-04.1 - Multifunction Display Lights

31-61-05A.title: EICAS Status Messages........................2.31-61-05.1 - System(s) Used
31-61-05A.remarks: May be inoperative provided a procedure is used before each flight to verify that associated equipment operates normally.
31-61-05A.maintenanceNote: Verify the associated equipment operates normally before each flight (AMM 31-00-00/901). NOTE: There is no acceptable procedure available for verifying the Flight Control System operates normally when the FLIGHT CONTROL SYS status message is displayed.
31-61-05A.operationsNote: Verify the associated equipment operates normally before each flight.

31-61-05B.title: EICAS Status Messages........................2.31-61-05.1 - System(s) Considered Inoperative
31-61-05B.remarks: May be inoperative provided associated equipment is considered inoperative.

31-61-06.title: Inboard Display Selector Positions
31-61-06.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Lower center display unit operates normally.
b. Remaining positions are verified to operate normally on associated selector.
c. Alternate procedures are used when required.
31-61-06.maintenanceNote: Verify that the inboard display (INBOARD DSPL) selector with the inoperative position operates normally in the remaining positions (AMM 31-00-00/901).
31-61-06.operationsNote:
Use alternate procedures if remaining display unit capability differs from established operator procedures. NOTE: AIMS display redundancy management will automatically provide PFD or EICAS formats to the proper display units when an associated outboard display unit failure or an upper center display unit failure is detected. Since the PFD and EICAS positions are not normally used, no alternate procedures are required when either or both positions are inoperative.
1. For an inoperative INBOARD DSPL selector in the NAV position, select the MFD position and select the desired MFD format on the associated inboard display unit using the DSP.
2. For an inoperative INBOARD DSPL selector in the MFD position, select the NAV position and use lower center display and opposite-side inboard display units for displaying required MFD formats.

31-61-07.title: Electronic Checklist (ECL) System
31-61-07.remarks: May be inoperative provided electronic checklist is deactivated and established suitable checklist procedures are used.
31-61-07.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the electronic checklist (AMM 31-00-00/901). NOTE: No maintenance action is required if the CHECKLIST DISABLED or CHECKLIST NOT AVAILABLE message is displayed on an MFD.
31-61-07.operationsNote: Use established paper checklists. NOTE 1: The rectangular icon symbol that precedes some alert messages will not be displayed. NOTE 2: When the ECL is disabled, the CHKL NON-NORMAL and CHKL INCOMPLETE NORM messages will not annunciate.

31-61-07-01.title: Electronic Checklist (ECL) System..........................................2.31-61-07.1 - ECL Closed Loop Switch Indications
31-61-07-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided ECL line item override procedures are used when required to complete checklists.
31-61-07-01.operationsNote: Use the Line Item Override (ITEM OVRD) Key as required.

31-61-08.title: EFIS Control Panels
31-61-08.remarks: One may be inoperative provided the associated CDU EFIS control panel backup feature is verified to operate normally.
31-61-08.maintenanceNote: Verify the associated (same side) CDU EFIS control backup feature operates normally (AMM 31-00-00/901).
31-61-08.operationsNote: Use associated (same side) CDU to control the functions of the inoperative EFIS control panel.

31-61-09-01.title: Instrument Source Switches.................................................2.31-61-09.1 - NAV and DSPL CTRL Switches
31-61-09-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided associated switches are not moved in flight.

31-61-09-02A.title: Instrument Source Switches.................................................2.31-61-09.1 - One Inoperative
31-61-09-02A.remarks: One may be inoperative provided the associated switch is not moved in flight.
31-61-09-02A.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
For AIMS Input/Output Module (IOM) #4 in the left AIMS cabinet inoperative,
selecting the left AIR DATA/ATT switch to the ALTN position will display failure
flags on the left PFD for attitude, airspeed and altitude. For IOM #2 in the right
AIMS cabinet inoperative, selecting the right AIR DATA/ATT switch to the ALTN
position will display an attitude fail flag on the right PFD.

31-61-09-02B.title: Instrument Source Switches.................................................2.31-61-09.1 - Both Inoperative
31-61-09-02B.remarks:
a. One AIR DATA/ATT switch is in the normal position.
b. Associated display units are verified to operate from selected sources.
c. Associated switches are not moved in flight.
31-61-09-02B.maintenanceNote: Verify display units operate from selected sources (AMM 31-00-00/901). NOTE: For AIMS Input/Output Module (IOM) #4 in the left AIMS cabinet inoperative, selecting the left AIR DATA/ATT switch to the ALTN position will display failure flags on the left PFD for attitude, airspeed and altitude. For IOM #2 in the right AIMS cabinet inoperative, selecting the right AIR DATA/ATT switch to the ALTN position will display an attitude fail flag on the right PFD.

31-61-10.title: Ground Maneuver Camera System (-300/-300ER)
31-61-10.remarks: May be inoperative provided repairs are made within 60 calendar days
31-61-10.operationsNote: Any operative portion of the camera system may be used.

31-61-11-01.title: Heading Reference (HDG REF) Switch.............................................2.31-61-11.1 - TRUE Function
31-61-11-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided enroute or contingency procedures including diversion airports do not require its use.
31-61-11-01.operationsNote: Operation is not allowed in routes where True North referencing is required.

32-00-01.title: Landing Gear Synoptic Display
32-00-01.operationsNote: If the Synoptic Display is missing data, selecting an alternate location for the display (L INBD, LWR CTR, or R INBD) may restore the missing data. Synoptic Displays containing missing data may continue to be used to the extent remaining data is useful. Airplane system faults will be annunciated by alerting and status messages.

32-08-01A.title: Proximity Sensor Electronic Unit (PSEU) Channels.................................................2.32-08-01.1 - One Inoperative - PSEU 1
32-08-01A.remarks: One may be inoperative in PSEU 1 provided the flight lock system is considered inoperative.
32-08-01A.operationsNote: NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 52-11-05.

32-08-01B.title: Proximity Sensor Electronic Unit (PSEU) Channels.................................................2.32-08-01.1 - One Inoperative - PSEU 2
32-08-01B.remarks: One may be inoperative in PSEU 2.

32-08-01C.title: Proximity Sensor Electronic Unit (PSEU) Channels.................................................2.32-08-01.1 - Two Inoperative - PSEU 1 On Right System Bus, PSEU 2 On Left System Bus
32-08-01C.remarks:
One may be inoperative in each PSEU provided:
a. PSEU 1 transmission is verified on the left ARINC 629 systems bus.
b. PSEU 2 transmission is verified on the right ARINC 629 systems bus.
c. Flight lock system is considered inoperative.
32-08-01C.maintenanceNote: Verify PSEU 1 transmission is on the left ARINC 629 systems bus and PSEU 2 transmission is on the right ARINC 629 systems bus (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-08-01C.operationsNote:
NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 52-11-05.

The autobrake selector may not automatically move from RTO to OFF after takeoff. If autobrake selector remains in RTO, manually move to OFF.

32-08-01D.title: Proximity Sensor Electronic Unit (PSEU) Channels.................................................2.32-08-01.1 - Two Inoperative - PSEU 1 On Left System Bus, PSEU 2 On Right System Bus
32-08-01D.remarks:
One may be inoperative in each PSEU provided:
a. PSEU 1 transmission is verified on the right ARINC 629 systems bus.
b. PSEU 2 transmission is verified on the left ARINC 629 systems bus.
c. After takeoff, gear remains down for two minutes before retraction.
d. Takeoff performance is based on landing gear extended.
e. Flight lock system is considered inoperative.
32-08-01D.maintenanceNote: Verify that PSEU 1 transmission is on the right ARINC 629 systems bus and PSEU 2 transmission is on the left ARINC 629 systems bus (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-08-01D.operationsNote:
NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 52-11-05.

1. The autobrake selector may not automatically move from RTO to OFF after takeoff. If autobrake selector remains in RTO, manually move to OFF.
2. After takeoff, leave the landing gear extended for a minimum of two minutes to allow the wheels to spin down prior to gear retraction.
3. Increase flight planning fuel by 861 kg. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-08-01E.title: Proximity Sensor Electronic Unit (PSEU) Channels.................................................2.32-08-01.1 - Two Inoperative - Gear Down Dispatch
32-08-01E.remarks:
One may be inoperative in each PSEU provided:
a. Landing gear are secured in the down position.
b. Airplane is dispatched in accordance with the appropriate AFM Gear Extended Appendix.
c. Flight lock system is considered inoperative.
32-08-01E.maintenanceNote: Secure the landing gear in the down position (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-08-01E.operationsNote:
NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 52-11-05.

1. The autobrake selector may not automatically move from RTO to OFF after takeoff. If autobrake selector remains in RTO, manually move to OFF.
2. Observe Landing Gear Extended certificate limitations and operational limits. NOTE: Dispatch requires authorization by CX Flight Operations Duty Manager and IOC in accordance with Landing Gear Extended.
3. Flight is limited to 50 miles from land.
4. Base flight plan on landing gear extended.
5. The Warning Electronics System (WES) will set VMO/MMO to 270 KIAS/.73 Mach and VMO GEAR DOWN memo message will be displayed. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-09-01-01.title: Air/Ground System - Weight on Wheels..................................2.32-09-01.1 - Left System
32-09-01-01.remarks:
a. Associated system is deactivated.
b. Right air/ground system operates normally.
c. Right system cardfile power supply 1 operates normally.
32-09-01-01.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the left Air/Ground System (AMM 32-00-00/901). NOTE: The WINDSHEAR SYS advisory message and WINDSHEAR PRED status message may be displayed. The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 34-43-01-01.
32-09-01-01.operationsNote: If available, select the right ATC transponder.

32-09-01-02.title: Air/Ground System - Weight on Wheels..................................2.32-09-01.1 - Right System
32-09-01-02.remarks:
a. Associated system is deactivated.
b. Left air/ground system operates normally.
c. All galley/lavatory water supply shutoff valves are closed.
32-09-01-02.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the right Air/Ground System and shutoff the water supply to the galley sinks, lavatory sinks and if installed drinking fountains (AMM 32-00-00/901). NOTE 1: The forward and aft drain mast heaters and the gray water drain line heaters default to low heat. Low heat inflight is likely to result in ice plugging drain masts or lines which can cause overflowing sinks. The left and right WOW cards are interchangeable (AMM 20-10-01/401). NOTE 2: The WINDSHEAR SYS advisory message and WINDSHEAR PRED status message may be displayed. The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 34-43-01-01.
32-09-01-02.operationsNote:
1. If available, select the left ATC transponder.
2. Water for the galley sinks, lavatory sinks and drinking fountains (if installed) will not be available.

32-11-01.title: Nose Landing Gear Strut Upper Air Chamber Pressure Indicator (-300ER)

32-30-01.title: Landing Gear Actuation System
32-30-01.remarks:
a. Inoperative components are properly secured by an accepted procedure.
b. Landing gear is secured in the down position.
c. Airplane is dispatched in accordance with Landing Gear Extended.
32-30-01.maintenanceNote: Secure the landing gear in the down position (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-30-01.operationsNote:
1. Observe Landing Gear Extended certificate limitations and operational limits. NOTE: Dispatch requires authorization by CX Flight Operations Duty Manager and IOC in accordance with Landing Gear Extended.
2. Flight is limited to 50 miles from land.
3. Base flight plan on landing gear extended.
4. The Warning Electronics System (WES) will set VMO/MMO to 270 KIAS/.73 Mach and VMO GEAR DOWN memo message will be displayed. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-30-02.title: Semi-Lever Gear (SLG) System (-300ER)
32-30-02.remarks:
a. SLG system is deactivated.
b. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
32-30-02.operationsNote: Dispatch with appropriate performance adjustments applied. NOTE: The SEMI LEVER GEAR SYS status message will remain displayed with the LEFT and RIGHT SEMI-LEVER GEAR CONTROL circuit breakers open. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-31-01.title: Landing Gear Lever Lock Solenoid
32-31-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided solenoid is in the locked position.
32-31-01.operationsNote:
For gear retraction use the following procedure.
1. Push and hold landing gear Lever LOCK OVRD switch.
2. Position Landing Gear Lever to UP.

32-31-02.title: Landing Gear Selector Valve Electrical Control Circuits
32-31-02.remarks: One UP/DOWN electrical control circuit may be inoperative provided the remaining UP/DOWN circuit is verified to operate normally each calendar day.
32-31-02.maintenanceNote: Verify that one of the electrical control circuits operates normally each calendar day (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-31-02.operationsNote: False TOO LOW GEAR aural alerts may occur. Confirm landing gear configuration. The aural caution may be inhibited by positioning the Ground Proximity Gear Override switch to OVRD.

32-32-01.title: Main Gear Door Uplock Spring Assemblies
32-32-01.remarks: One spring on each door uplock mechanism may be missing and gear retraction allowed provided 270 KIAS/.82 Mach is not exceeded during flight.
32-32-01.maintenanceNote: Remove any pieces of broken spring (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-32-01.operationsNote: Observe the landing gear EXTEND placard (270K - .82M) speed limit during all phases of flight.

32-32-01-01.title: Main Gear Door Uplock Spring Assemblies.................................2.32-32-01.1 - Spring Retention Cords

32-32-02.title: Main Gear Uplock Springs
32-32-02.remarks: One spring on one main gear uplock mechanism may be missing and gear retraction allowed provided 270 KIAS/.82 Mach is not exceeded during flight.
32-32-02.maintenanceNote: Remove any pieces of broken spring (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-32-02.operationsNote: Observe the landing gear EXTEND placard (270K - .82M) speed limit during all phases of flight.

32-35-01.title: Landing Gear Alternate Extend System
32-35-01.remarks:
a. Landing gear are secured in the down position.
b. Alternate extend system is deactivated.
c. Airplane is dispatched in accordance with the appropriate AFM Gear Extended Appendix.
32-35-01.maintenanceNote: Deactivate alternate extend system and secure the landing gear in the down position (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-35-01.operationsNote:
1. Observe Landing Gear Extended certificate limitations and operational limits. NOTE: Dispatch requires authorization by CX Flight Operations Duty Manager and IOC in accordance with AFM Landing Gear Extended Appendix.
2. Flight is limited to 50 miles from land.
3. Base flight plan on landing gear extended.
4. The Warning Electronics System (WES) will set VMO/MMO to 270 KIAS/.73 Mach and VMO GEAR DOWN memo message will be displayed. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-35-01-01.title: Landing Gear Alternate Extend System.......................................2.32-35-01.1 - Alternate Extend Hydraulic Pressure Switch
32-35-01-01.remarks:
a. Inoperative pressure switch is open.
b. Landing gear doors are verified to open using the alternate extend system.
32-35-01-01.maintenanceNote: Verify the landing gear doors open using the alternate extend system (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-35-01-01.operationsNote: For Non-Normal Checklists that use the alternate gear extend system, the gear should indicate in-transit within approximately 16 seconds.

32-35-02.title: Ground Door Release Control System
32-35-02.remarks:
a. Both door open control switches are verified to be open.
b. Landing gear doors are verified to open using the alternate extend system.
c. Landing gear doors are closed before each departure.
32-35-02.maintenanceNote: Verify both door open control switches are open (not inoperative closed) and the landing gear doors will open using the alternate extend switch on the flight deck (AMM 32-00-00/901).

32-35-02-01.title: Ground Door Release Control System......................................2.32-35-02.1 - Door Open Control Switches
32-35-02-01.remarks:
a. Inoperative control switch(s) is closed.
b. Landing gear are secured in the down position.
c. Landing gear alternate extend system is deactivated.
d. Airplane is dispatched in accordance with the appropriate AFM Gear Extended Appendix.
32-35-02-01.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the gear alternate extend system and secure the landing gear down (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-35-02-01.operationsNote:
1. Observe Landing Gear Extended certificate limitations and operational limits. NOTE: Dispatch requires authorization by the CX Flight Operations Duty Manager and IOC in accordance with Landing Gear Extended.
2. Flight is limited to 50 miles from land.
3. Base flight plan on landing gear extended.
4. The Warning Electronics System (WES) will set VMO/MMO to 270 KIAS/.73 Mach and VMO GEAR DOWN memo message will be displayed. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-41-01.title: Brake Accumulator Pressure Indicator (Wheel Well)
32-41-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided flight deck brake accumulator pressure indicator operates normally.

32-41-02.title: Brake Accumulator Pressure Indicator (Flight Deck)
32-41-02.remarks: May be inoperative provided brake accumulator charge is verified normal once each calendar day.
32-41-02.maintenanceNote: Verify brake accumulator precharge pressure once each calendar day (AMM 32-00-00/901).

32-41-03.title: BRAKE SOURCE Indication System
32-41-03.remarks:
a. Flight deck brake accumulator pressure indicator operates normally.
b. Normal and alternate brake systems are verified to operate normally.
c. Brake accumulator isolation valve is verified to operate normally.
d. Alternate procedures are established and used.
e. Repairs are made within 3 calendar days.
32-41-03.maintenanceNote: Verify normal and alternate brake systems, and brake accumulator isolation valve operate normally (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-41-03.operationsNote:
Establish alternate procedures.
1. During taxi and landing operations, monitor the brake accumulator pressure indicator.
2. If the brake accumulator pressure is less than 2800 psi for longer than three seconds, accomplish the BRAKE SOURCE Non-Normal Checklist.

32-41-03-01.title: BRAKE SOURCE Indication System..................................2.32-41-03.1 - BRAKE SOURCE Light
32-41-03-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided the BRAKE SOURCE alerting message operates normally.
32-41-03-01.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
The BRAKE SOURCE advisory message will not operate for towing operations
conducted without AC electrical power applied to the airplane.

32-42-01A.title: Normal Antiskid Valves.........................2.32-42-01.1 - Deactivation Tool Used
32-42-01A.remarks:
One valve per each six wheel truck may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated brake is deactivated using the deactivation assembly.
b. Performance decrements for brake(s) deactivated are applied.
32-42-01A.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the brake associated with inoperative antiskid valve (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-42-01A.operationsNote:
NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 32-45-01A.

Dispatch with takeoff and landing performance based on one or two brakes deactivated. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-42-01B.title: Normal Antiskid Valves.........................2.32-42-01.1 - Brake Line Capped
32-42-01B.remarks:
One valve per each six wheel truck may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated brake is deactivated by capping the brake line.
b. After takeoff, gear remains down for two minutes before retraction.
c. Performance decrements for brake(s) deactivated are applied.
d. Takeoff performance is based on landing gear extended.
32-42-01B.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the brake associated with inoperative antiskid valve (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-42-01B.operationsNote:
NOTE: Airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 32-45-01B.

1. After takeoff, leave the landing gear extended for a minimum of two minutes to allow the wheels to spin down prior to gear retraction.
2. Base takeoff performance on landing gear extended.
3. Dispatch with takeoff and landing performance also based on one or two brakes deactivated.
4. Increase flight planning fuel by 861 kg. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-42-02.title: Antiskid Wheelspeed Transducers
32-42-02.remarks:
One transducer per each six wheel truck may be inoperative provided:
a. Performance decrements for brake(s) deactivated are applied.
b. No other brakes are deactivated on that truck.
32-42-02.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
Brakes associated with inoperative transducers are not required to be
deactivated.

Dispatch with takeoff and landing performance based on one or two brakes deactivated. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-42-03.title: Alternate Antiskid Valves
32-42-03.remarks: May be inoperative provided manual braking capability on the alternate brake system is verified to operate normally.
32-42-03.maintenanceNote: Verify that pedal braking capability operates normally (AMM 32-00-00/901).

32-42-04A.title: Autobrake System (Including Autobrake Solenoid Valve)......................................2.32-42-04.1 - Solenoid Verified Closed
32-42-04A.remarks:
a. Autobrake solenoid valve is verified closed.
b. Autobrake selector remains in the OFF position.
32-42-04A.maintenanceNote: Verify that the autobrake solenoid valve is closed and for Brake System Control Unit II (BSCU II) installed, check the program pin configuration (AMM 32-00-00/901). NOTE: If AUTOBRAKE SOL VALVE Status message is displayed, the autobrake valve module must be deactivated for dispatch. Refer to MEL item 32-42-04B. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-42-04B.title: Autobrake System (Including Autobrake Solenoid Valve)......................................2.32-42-04.1 - Control Module Deactivated
32-42-04B.remarks:
a. Autobrake hydraulic control module is deactivated.
b. Autobrake selector remains in the OFF position.
32-42-04B.maintenanceNote: Deactivate the autobrake hydraulic control module and for Brake System Control Unit II (BSCU II) installed, check the program pin configuration (AMM 32-00-00/901). COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-44-01B.title: Brake Status Lights (On Nose Gear)..............................................2.32-44-01.1 - Procedures Do Not Require Use
32-44-01B.remarks: May be inoperative provided procedures do not require their use.
32-44-01B.operationsNote:
COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE
Normal operating procedures do not require the use of the Brake Status Light

32-44-02.title: Gear Retraction Braking System
32-44-02.remarks:
a. After takeoff, gear remains down for two minutes before retraction.
b. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied. NOTE: In the event of engine failure after V1, retract landing gear after takeoff.
32-44-02.operationsNote:
NOTE: It is not necessary to apply landing gear extended takeoff performance adjustments.
1. Increase flight planning fuel by 861 kg.
2. After takeoff, leave the landing gear extended for a minimum of two minutes to allow the wheels to spin down prior to gear retraction.
3. In case of engine failure after V1, landing gear should be retracted after takeoff. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-44-03.title: Parking Brake Set Indication System (Flight Deck)
32-44-03.remarks:
a. Alternate procedures are established and used.
b. Parking brake valve is verified to operate normally once each calendar day.
c. Parking brake and brake antiskid interface indication is verified to operate normally once each calendar day.
d. Parking brake takeoff configuration warning system is verified to operate normally.
32-44-03.maintenanceNote: Verify the parking brake takeoff configuration warning operates normally and verify once each calendar day the parking brake valve, the parking brake and the brake antiskid interface indication operate normally (AMM 32-00-00/901). NOTE: This MEL item is for PARKING BRAKE SET memo message not displayed when the parking brake lever is set.
32-44-03.operationsNote: Alternate procedures require communication between flight crew and ground crew to confirm park brake status. Flight crew must manually confirm the position of the park brake lever.

32-45-01A.title: Wheel Brakes.........................................2.32-45-01.1 - Deactivation Tool Used
32-45-01A.remarks:
One per each six wheel truck may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated brake is deactivated with a deactivation assembly.
b. Performance decrements for brakes deactivated are applied.
32-45-01A.maintenanceNote: Deactivate associated brake using the Deactivation Assembly (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-45-01A.operationsNote: Dispatch with takeoff and landing performance based on one or two brakes deactivated. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-45-01B.title: Wheel Brakes.........................................2.32-45-01.1 - Brake Line Capped
32-45-01B.remarks:
One per each six wheel truck may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated brake is deactivated by capping the brake line.
b. After takeoff, gear remains down for two minutes before retraction.
c. Performance decrements for brakes deactivated are applied.
d. Takeoff performance is based on landing gear extended.
32-45-01B.maintenanceNote: Deactivate inoperative brake by capping the associated brake line (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-45-01B.operationsNote:
1. After takeoff, leave the landing gear extended for a minimum of two minutes to allow the wheels to spin down prior to gear retraction.
2. Base takeoff performance on landing gear extended.
3. Dispatch with takeoff and landing performance also based on one or two brakes deactivated.
4. Increase flight planning fuel by 861 kg. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-45-01C.title: Wheel Brakes.........................................2.32-45-01.1 - Center Axle Brake Removed
32-45-01C.remarks:
One per each six wheel truck may be removed from the center axle only provided:
a. Associated brake line is capped.
b. After takeoff, gear remains down for two minutes before retraction.
c. Performance decrements for brakes deactivated are applied.
d. Takeoff performance is based on landing gear extended.
32-45-01C.maintenanceNote: Remove inoperative brake and cap the associated brake line (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-45-01C.operationsNote:
1. After takeoff, leave the landing gear extended for a minimum of two minutes to allow the wheels to spin down prior to gear retraction.
2. Base takeoff performance on landing gear extended.
3. Dispatch with takeoff and landing performance also based on one or two brakes deactivated.
4. Increase flight planning fuel by 861 kg. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-45-02.title: Wheel Tie Bolts
32-45-02.remarks:
One per wheel may be broken or missing provided:
a. Affected wheel is removed, checked for broken parts or damage, and replaced if broken parts or damage is found.
b. Associated brake is checked for broken parts or damage, and is replaced or deactivated if broken parts or damage is found.
c. After each landing, wheel is inspected for additional broken or missing tie bolts.
d. Operations are limited to five departures before repairs are made.
32-45-02.maintenanceNote: Remove the wheel and tire assembly, and inspect the wheel and brake assemblies for broken parts or damage. Inspect the wheel after each landing and replace the affected wheel after five departures (AMM 32-00-00/901).

32-45-04.title: Nose Gear Spin Brake
32-45-04.remarks:
May be inoperative or missing provided:
a. After takeoff, gear remains down for two minutes before retraction.
b. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied. NOTE: In the event of engine failure after V1, retract landing gear after takeoff.
32-45-04.operationsNote:
NOTE: It is not necessary to apply landing gear extended takeoff performance adjustments.
1. Increase flight planning fuel by 861 kg.
2. After takeoff, leave the landing gear extended for a minimum of two minutes prior to gear retraction.
3. In case of engine failure after V1, landing gear should be retracted after takeoff. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT item.

32-46-01.title: Brake Temperature Indication System
32-46-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided Maximum Quick Turnaround Weight limitations are observed. NOTE: Any portion of the system that operates normally may be used.
32-46-01.operationsNote: Observe Maximum Quick Turnaround Weight limitation in FCOM V1 Performance Dispatch – Landing.

32-49-01A.title: Tire Pressure Indication System....................................................2.32-49-01.1 - Required By Procedures
32-49-01A.remarks: May be inoperative provided alternate procedures are established and used. NOTE: Any portion of the system that operates normally may be used.
32-49-01A.maintenanceNote: For tire pressure check Scheduled Maintenance Task, use a tire pressure gauge to measure tire pressure (AMM 32-00-00/901)

32-53-01.title: Main Gear Steering System (Including Indication)
32-53-01.remarks:
a. Main gear steering actuators are verified locked in the center position.
b. Main gear steering system is deactivated.
32-53-01.maintenanceNote: Verify that both main gear steering actuators are locked in the center position and deactivate the main gear steering system (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-53-01.operationsNote:
1. There is negligible change in U-turn widths if the Flight Crew Training Manual Pivot Turn Technique is used.
2. Minimum radius turns will result in the following effects: A. Substantially increased tire scuffing. B. Increased thrust required for the turn. C. Somewhat rougher cabin ride, particularly in the area above the main gear.

32-61-01.title: Landing Gear Position Indication Systems
32-61-01.remarks:
a. Landing gear are secured in the down position.
b. Airplane is dispatched in accordance with Landing Gear Extended.
32-61-01.maintenanceNote: Secure the landing gear in the down position (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-61-01.operationsNote:
1. Observe Landing Gear Extended certificate limitations and operational limits. NOTE: Dispatch requires authorization by CX Flight Operations Duty Manager and IOC in accordance with Landing Gear Extended.
2. Base flight plan on landing gear extended.
3. Flight is limited to 50 miles from land.
4. The Warning Electronics System (WES) will set VMO/MMO to 270 KIAS/.73 Mach and the VMO GEAR DOWN memo message will be displayed. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-61-01-01.title: Landing Gear Position Indication Systems................................2.32-61-01.1 - Truck Tilt Sensors
32-61-01-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided the nose gear lock, nose gear down, main gear side brace and main gear drag brace sensors are verified to operate normally each calendar day.
32-61-01-01.maintenanceNote: Verify the nose gear lock, nose gear down, main gear side brace and main gear drag brace sensors operate normally each calendar day (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-61-01-01.operationsNote:
NOTE 1: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 27-62-01.
NOTE 2: An inoperative truck tilt sensor will also result in the AUTO
SPEEDBRAKE advisory and status messages being displayed. The
AUTO SPEEDBRAKE messages may not display until all three
hydraulic systems are pressurized.

After takeoff manually move the autobrake selector from RTO to OFF.

32-61-01-02-01.title: Landing Gear Position Indication Systems................................2.32-61-01.1 - PSEU-1
32-61-01-02-01.remarks:
a. Nose gear lock, nose gear down, main gear side brace and main gear drag brace sensors are verified to operate normally each calendar day.
b. PSEU-2 operates normally.
32-61-01-02-01.maintenanceNote: Verify the nose gear lock, nose gear down, main gear side brace and main gear drag brace sensors operate normally each calendar day (AMM 32-00-00/901).

32-61-01-02-02.title: Landing Gear Position Indication Systems................................2.32-61-01.1 - PSEU-2
32-61-01-02-02.remarks:
a. Nose gear lock, nose gear down, main gear side brace and main gear drag brace sensors are verified to operate normally each calendar day.
b. Left equipment cooling controller operates normally.
c. PSEU-1 operates normally.
32-61-01-02-02.maintenanceNote: Verify the nose gear lock, nose gear down, main gear side brace and main gear drag brace sensors operate normally each calendar day (AMM 32-00-00/901).

32-61-02.title: Landing Gear Door Position Sensors
32-61-02.remarks: One per gear (nose, left main, right main) may be inoperative provided sensor is failed in the door not closed position.
32-61-02.maintenanceNote: Confirm inoperative sensors are not indicating the closed position (AMM 32-00-00/901).

32-61-03.title: Landing Gear Uplock Position Sensors
32-61-03.remarks: One per gear may be inoperative provided the sensor is failed in the unlocked position and the associated landing gear door position sensors operate normally.
32-61-03.maintenanceNote: Confirm inoperative sensors are not indicating the locked position (AMM 32-00-00/901).

32-71-01B.title: Tail Strike Detector Channels.................................................2.32-71-01.1 - Both Inoperative
32-71-01B.remarks:
a. Tail section is visually inspected for damage before each departure.
b. Alternate tail strike detection procedures are established and used.
c. TAIL STRIKE caution message is disabled.
32-71-01B.maintenanceNote: Disable the TAIL STRIKE caution message (AMM 32-00-00/901). NOTE: Before each departure, visually inspect the tail section of the aircraft for damage from a tail strike.
32-71-01B.operationsNote: NOTE: The TAIL STRIKE caution message is not available. During takeoff and flare, flight crew and cabin crew should be alert for a potential tail strike. If a tail strike is perceived by the flight crew or reported from the cabin during takeoff, do the Tail Strike Non-Normal Checklist.

32-72-01.title: Tail Skid (-300/-300ER) 32-72-01-02 -300ER (If Installed)
32-72-01.remarks:
a. Tail skid is secured in the extended position.
b. Water supplies associated with aft drain mast are secured off.
c. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
32-72-01.maintenanceNote: Secure tail skid in the fully extended position and secure water supplies associated with the aft drain mast off (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-72-01.operationsNote:
NOTE: The tail skid system is not installed on -300ER airplanes B-KQM
onwards and is being progressively removed from earlier airplanes for
weight savings.

1. Reduce performance limited weights by the appropriate adjustments. Performance Limited Weights Takeoff & Landing Enroute Climb -300ER 680 kg 1,588 kg a. 3.00-01-00.2 in the ENROUTE DIVERSION SPEED EFFECTS paragraph
2. Increase flight planning fuel by
1.0%. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-72-02-01A.title: Tail Skid Position Sensing System (-300/-300ER)..........................................2.32-72-02.1 32-72-02-01 -300.....................................................2.32-72-02.1 - Tail Skid Operative
32-72-02-01A.remarks: May be inoperative provided tail skid extend/retract function is verified to operate normally once each calendar day.
32-72-02-01A.maintenanceNote: Verify the tail skid extend/retract function operates normally each calendar day (AMM 32-00-00/901).

c. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.

The enroute climb weight penalties listed above are based on single engine operating speeds that approximate maximum lift-to-drag ratio speed. To account for the difference in level off altitude when operating at other speeds, multiply the enroute climb weight penalty listed above by the appropriate factor listed on page
3.00-01-00.2 in the ENROUTE DIVERSION SPEED EFFECTS paragraph
2. Increase flight planning fuel by
1.0%. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

32-72-02-02A.title: Tail Skid Position Sensing System (-300/-300ER)..........................................2.32-72-02.1 32-72-02-01 -300.....................................................2.32-72-02.1 - Tail Skid Operative
32-72-02-02A.remarks: May be inoperative provided tail skid extend/retract function is verified to operate normally once each calendar day.
32-72-02-02A.maintenanceNote: Verify the tail skid extend/retract function operates normally each calendar day (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-72-02-02A.operationsNote:
NOTE: The tail skid system is not installed on -300ER airplanes from B-KQM
onwards and B-HNR.

32-72-02-02B.title: Tail Skid Position Sensing System (-300/-300ER)..........................................2.32-72-02.1 32-72-02-01 -300.....................................................2.32-72-02.1 - Tail Skid Inoperative
32-72-02-02B.remarks:
a. Tail skid is secured in the extended position.
b. Water supplies associated with aft drain mast are secured off.
c. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
32-72-02-02B.maintenanceNote: Secure the tail skid in the extended position and secure water supplies associated with the aft drain mast off (AMM 32-00-00/901).
32-72-02-02B.operationsNote:
NOTE: The tail skid system is not installed on -300ER airplanes from B-KQM
