33-11-01.title: Flight Compartment and Instrument Lighting System
33-11-01.remarks:
Individual lights or light controls may be inoperative provided:
a. Remaining lighting system lights are sufficient to clearly illuminate all required instruments, controls, and other devices for which it is provided.
b. Remaining lighting system lights are positioned so that direct rays are shielded from flight crew eyes.
c. Lighting configuration and intensity is acceptable to the flight crew.
d. Captain’s emergency dome light operates normally. NOTE: Individual button/switch lights and/or annunciations/indications are excluded from this relief.
33-11-01.companyMaintenanceNote: The Captain’s dome light assembly contains the flight deck emergency lamp. With the DOME and STORM light switches OFF, emergency dome light operation can be verified by momentarily turning the EMER LIGHTS switch to ON.

33-11-01-01.title: Flight Compartment and Instrument Lighting System.....................................................2.33-11-01.1 - STORM Switch ON Light

33-13-01.title: Master Brightness Control
33-13-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided the master brightness control switch is selected off.

33-16-01.title: Master Dim and Test System
33-16-01.remarks:
Dim function may be inoperative provided:
a. TEST and BRT functions operate normally.
b. Light intensity is acceptable to the flight crew.
33-16-01.operationsNote: Only a portion of the flight deck annunciator lights may be affected. The light intensity must be deemed acceptable by each flight crew.

33-21-01-01-01.title: Cabin Interior Illumination.............................................2.33-21-01.1 - With Powered Floor Proximity Emergency Escape Path Lighting System
33-21-01-01-01.remarks:
Individual lights may be inoperative provided:
a. Sufficient lighting remains for crew members to perform their duties.
b. For night operations beyond 60 minutes of landing at a suitable airport, at least 75% of the standby lights operate normally.

33-24-01A.title: Passenger Information Signs (Passenger)..................................2.33-24-01.1 - PA System Inoperative
33-24-01A.remarks:
a. Associated passenger seat, or lavatory is not occupied from which a Passenger Information sign is not readily legible.
b. Associated seat or lavatory must be blocked and placarded - DO NOT OCCUPY. NOTE: These provisions are not intended to prohibit lavatory use or inspections by crewmembers.
33-24-01A.maintenanceNote: NOTE: In tests conducted at Boeing for the FAA, a sign was considered readily legible if enough of the sign could be seen to identify it. For example, NO SMOK and FASTEN SEAT B would be considered readily legible. Block and placard associated seat or close and lock associated lavatory (AMM 33-00-00/901).
33-24-01A.companyMaintenanceNote: Placard the affected seat 'DO NOT OCCUPY' (Placard P/N DNO1).
33-24-01A.operationsNote:
NOTE: In the event of any lavatory being locked closed, the aircraft must
also be dispatched using MEL item 25-45-01.

33-24-01B.title: Passenger Information Signs (Passenger)..................................2.33-24-01.1 - PA System Operative
33-24-01B.remarks:
May be inoperative and the associated passenger seat or lavatory may be occupied provided:
a. PA system operates normally and can be clearly heard throughout the cabin during flight.
b. PA system is used to alert the cabin crew and to notify passengers when seat belts should be fastened, when smoking is prohibited, and when passengers should return to seats.
33-24-01B.operationsNote: The flight crew shall use the PA system to alert the cabin crew and notify passengers when seat belts should be fastened and when passengers should return to seats.

33-24-01C.title: Passenger Information Signs (Passenger)..................................2.33-24-01.1 - No Passenger Carried
33-24-01C.remarks:
a. No passengers are carried.
b. A maximum of 19 persons authorized for non-passenger carrying operations are carried.
c. Alternate procedures are established and used.
33-24-01C.operationsNote:
1. No passengers may be carried.
2. A maximum of 19 authorized persons may be carried.
3. Alternate procedures require flight crew members and authorized passengers are briefed prior to takeoff and landing, that the Cabin Interphone system will be used for notification when seat belts must be used.

33-24-01-01.title: Passenger Information Signs (Passenger)..................................2.33-24-01.1 - Flight Deck Automatic Function
33-24-01-01.remarks:
a. Manual control function operates normally.
b. Alternate procedures are established and used.
33-24-01-01.operationsNote: Alternate procedures require that the Cabin Crew are briefed on the unserviceable equipment. PAs must be made as applicable to alert Cabin Crew and Passengers when seat belts are required to be fastened. NOTE 1: The No Smoking signs automatic function illuminates the NO SMOKING signs when landing gear not up and locked, or cabin altitude above 10,000 feet, or passenger oxygen on. For the 77J cabin configuration, the NO SMOKING signs are not electrically illuminated, they are visible at all times. NOTE 2: The Fasten Seat Belt signs automatic function illuminates the FASTEN SEAT BELT signs when landing gear not up and locked, or flap lever not up, or airplane altitude below an operator defined altitude, or cabin altitude above 10,000 feet, or passenger oxygen on.

33-24-01-02.title: Passenger Information Signs (Passenger)..................................2.33-24-01.1 - Crew/Attendant Rest Areas
33-24-01-02.remarks: May be inoperative provided alternate procedures are established and used.
33-24-01-02.operationsNote: Alternate procedures require that the PA system is used to notify crew/attendant rest occupants when seat belts should be fastened

33-24-01-03.title: Passenger Information Signs (Passenger)..................................2.33-24-01.1 - Aural Tone Function
33-24-01-03.remarks: May be inoperative provided alternate procedures are established and used.
33-24-01-03.operationsNote: Alternate procedures require that the SCCM is briefed that notification by cabin interphone will be used whenever the Fasten Seat Belt signs are selected on.

33-31-01A.title: Service Area Lights (Main Wheel Well, Nose Wheel Well, Air Conditioning Compartment, APU Compartment, Stabilizer Compartment, Electrical Equipment Center).................................2.33-31-01.1 - All Operations

33-37-01.title: Cargo Compartment Lights
33-37-01.remarks: Individual lights may be inoperative provided sufficient lighting remains for ground personnel to perform their duties.

33-41-01-01.title: Wing Illumination Lights.......................2.33-41-01.1 - WING Switch ON Light

33-42-01.title: Taxi Lights
33-42-01.companyMaintenanceNote: If desired, this item may be applied for an inoperative Taxi Light due to a cracked Taxi Light lens (AMM 33-42-03/201).

33-42-02A.title: Landing Lights.......................................2.33-42-02.1 - All Operations
33-42-02A.remarks: Two may be inoperative for night operations.

33-42-02B.title: Landing Lights.......................................2.33-42-02.1 - Day Operations
33-42-02B.remarks: May be inoperative provided operations are not conducted at night.

33-43-01A.title: Position Lights.......................................2.33-43-01.1 - All Operations
33-43-01A.remarks:
a. One stationary red wing tip bulb operates normally.
b. One stationary green wing tip bulb operates normally.
c. One stationary white bulb per wing tip operates normally.

33-43-01B.title: Position Lights.......................................2.33-43-01.1 - Day Operations
33-43-01B.remarks: May be inoperative between sunrise and sunset.

33-44-01-01A.title: Anti-Collision Lights..............................2.33-44-01.1 - All Operations
33-44-01-01A.remarks: May be inoperative provided white tail and wing tip strobe lights operate normally.
33-44-01-01A.companyMaintenanceNote: Notify all onward stations (Engineering and Traffic) and HKG IOC that the aircraft is operating with the lower anti-collision beacon inoperative so appropriate ramp safety measures can be taken on arrival (Note: When the defect has been entered into the system, all down route stations are advised of all incoming MEL items).

33-44-01-01B.title: Anti-Collision Lights..............................2.33-44-01.1 - Day Operations
33-44-01-01B.remarks:
a. At least one white tail or wing tip strobe light operates normally.
b. Operations are not conducted at night.
33-44-01-01B.companyMaintenanceNote: Notify all onward stations (Engineering and Traffic) and HKG IOC that the aircraft is operating with the lower anti-collision beacon inoperative so appropriate ramp safety measures can be taken on arrival (Note: When the defect has been entered into the system, all down route stations are advised of all incoming MEL items).

33-44-01-02A.title: Anti-Collision Lights..............................2.33-44-01.1 - All Operations
33-44-01-02A.remarks: May be inoperative provided red upper and lower fuselage beacon lights operate normally.

33-44-01-02B.title: Anti-Collision Lights..............................2.33-44-01.1 - Day Operations
33-44-01-02B.remarks:
a. At least one red fuselage beacon light operates normally.
b. Operations are not conducted at night.

33-47-01.title: Ground Maneuvering Camera System Lights
33-47-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided repairs are made within 60 days.
33-47-01.operationsNote: NOTE: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 31-61-10.

33-51-01.title: Interior Emergency Lights
33-51-01.remarks:
A random 25% of lights/signs may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative area illumination lights are not adjacent.
b. Not more than one overhead area light or exit sign at each door is inoperative.
c. Cross-aisle exit signs operate normally.
d. Flight deck emergency dome light operates normally. NOTE: Lights associated with an inoperative door or slide/raft are not required.
33-51-01.companyMaintenanceNote: The Captain’s dome light assembly contains the flight deck emergency lamp. With the DOME and STORM light switches OFF, emergency dome light operation can be verified by momentarily turning the EMER LIGHTS switch to ON.
33-51-01.operationsNote: 1. the following are the minimum dispatch requirements for an exit sign to be considered operative: A. Horizontal exit signs - At least 9 of 12 lamps must be operative. B. Vertical exit signs - At least 3 of 5 lamps must be operative.

33-51-02.title: Exterior Emergency Slide Lights
33-51-02.remarks: May be inoperative provided operations are not conducted at night.

33-51-02-02-01.title: Exterior Emergency Slide Lights......................................................2.33-51-02.1 33-51-02-02 -300/-300ER........................................2.33-51-02.1 - Doors 1L, 1R, 2L, 2R, 4L, 4R, 5L and 5R
33-51-02-02-01.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated passenger entry door is considered inoperative.
b. Exterior emergency slide lights for doors 3L and 3R operate normally.
c. Repairs are made within 1 calendar day.
33-51-02-02-01.operationsNote: The airplane must also be dispatched using MEL item 52-11-01.

33-51-02-02-02.title: Exterior Emergency Slide Lights......................................................2.33-51-02.1 33-51-02-02 -300/-300ER........................................2.33-51-02.1 - Doors 3L and 3R
33-51-02-02-02.remarks:
Lights associated with one door may be inoperative provided:
a. Associated passenger entry door is considered inoperative.
b. All remaining door exterior emergency slide lights operate normally.

34-16-01.title: Altitude Alerting System
34-16-01.remarks:
a. Autopilot with altitude hold and altitude capture operates normally.
b. Enroute operations do not require its use.
c. Repairs are made within 3 calendar days.
d. One altitude alerting system is required to be operative for RVSM and NAT- HLA operations.
e. Aircraft shall not depart Hong Kong unless the flight does not require passing over any other airspace.
34-16-01.operationsNote:
1. Enroute operations that require RVSM and NAT-HLA may not be conducted.
2. Use the autopilot and altitude hold for all operations for which it is appropriate.
3. Cross-check the MCP ALTITUDE window with altitude indications on captain’s and first officer’s PFDs upon reaching and departing an assigned altitude. Periodically cross-check altitude indications when maintaining an assigned altitude.
4. Pilot monitoring should call out approaching and departing assigned altitudes.
5. Flight crew must be aware that the usual alerts for altitude deviations will not occur. 34-61-01-03.remarks:
May be out of date for 3 consecutive calendar days provided that:
a. The procedures of the out-of-date navigation database changed in the current navigation database are not used (the procedures not changed may be used), and
b. Alternate procedures are established and used, and
c. The current aeronautical information (e.g. charts) is used to check the database navigation fixes (the coordinates, frequencies, status (as applicable)), and suitability of navigation facilities required for the intended route, and
d. That the navigation database is valid for all flights departing HKG including valid for the duration of the flight. NOTE: A return flight to HKG may be authorized provided approval to operate is obtained from IOC/Navigation Services prior to dispatch.
34-61-01-03.operationsNote:
For PBN operations: The FMCS navigation database must be current for PBN operations unless verifies acceptable by the COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE procedure. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE To verify that the out-of-date database is the equivalent of the current database for the intended return flight:
1. IOC/Navigation Services verify the intended return Flight Plan is not subject to changes incorporated in the new Navigation Database cycle.
2. Approved current Aeronautical Charts and NOTAMs are used to verify all Flight Plan Waypoints and navigation fixes against the FM loaded route prior to dispatch.
3. Verify approach navigation radios are properly tuned and identified.
4. IF the MEL item has been raised after the ATC flight plan has been received, contact Flight Dispatch via IOC to verify that the ATC Flight Plan reflects the current aircraft equipment capability based on the MEL item. If the navigation database procedure intended to be flown is identical to the current aeronautical information (charts): Use the procedure of the out of date navigation database. If the navigation database procedure intended to be flown is not identical to the current aeronautical information (charts): - For conventional SID, STAR, APPR procedures, use the procedure intended to be flown by manually tuning the radio navigation aids (VOR, DME, ADF, ILS), or request the assistance of the Air Navigation Service Providers. - For En route operations, insert new routings according to the current airways.

36-12-01A.operationsNote:

1. For EDTO flight planning, increase the engine inoperative Critical Fuel Reserves by
1.3% when dispatching into known or forecast icing conditions.

After takeoff is completed, position the operative ISLN switch AUTO (inoperative ISLN switch remains CLOSED) and configure the APU as required. 49-42-01A.title: APU Starting System (Includes Electric Starter).....................2.49-42-01.1 - APU Required
49-42-01A.remarks: May be dispatched with APU START SYS faults provided APU is started before departure and operated continuously throughout the flight.
49-42-01A.companyMaintenanceNote: This MEL item requires additional fuel uplift, and is only to be used when the APU is required for other MEL procedures as listed under 49-42-01B, or if dispatch requires greater than 180 minutes EDTO.
49-42-01A.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
Some electric starter failures may result in damage to the APU if it is used. If the
APU fails to start electrically but starts pneumatically, the possibility of APU
damage can be reduced by doing the following steps.
1. Perform the APU Magnetic Chip Collector Inspection (AMM Task
49-27-04/201).
2. If the Chip Collector Inspection is satisfactory:
A. Position Overhead Maintenance Panel (P61) APU Maintenance
switch NORM.
B. Position Overhead Panel (P5) APU selector OFF.
C. Remove the end cap from the electric starter motor on the APU.
D. Use a socket and ratchet on the shaft for the electric starter to turn the
APU counterclockwise, facing aft.
1) The APU should turn freely. Verify the APU is turning freely by
visual inspection of the power section compressor blades
through the bottom access panel of the APU inlet duct (AMM
49-21-00/Figure 601).
2) If the APU does not turn freely, serious damage can occur if the
APU is operated (see FIM Chapter 49-40, Task 812, Fault
Isolation Procedure - Mechanical Fault).
E. Remove the socket and ratchet, and re-install the end cap on the
electric starter.

1. Increase flight planning fuel by
2.5% to account for the open APU air inlet door. Also increase flight planning fuel by 90 kg per hour of APU usage in- flight and 240 kg per hour of APU usage on the ground.
2. Start the APU before departure and operate the APU continuously throughout the flight. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE
1. This MEL item is applied if dispatch greater than 180min EDTO is required however, as the APU is required to be running throughout the flight resulting in increased flight plan fuel and APU running hours it is preferred to downgrade the aircraft to 180 EDTO using item 49-42-01B.
2. Dispatch with this item is required if the APU is required for other MEL items as listed in the item 49-42-01B OPERATIONS (O) procedure.

52-11-01-01A.title: Main Entry Doors/Slides.........................2.52-11-01.1 - Passengers Carried
52-11-01-01A.remarks:
One door/slide may be inoperative or slide missing provided:
a. All other main entry doors are fully operational.
b. Affected door is not used for passenger loading.
c. A conspicuous barrier strap or rope and a placard stating that the door is inoperative shall be placed across the inoperative door.
d. Emergency exit sign and floor proximity lights associated with the inoperative exit must be covered to obscure the sign and lights.
e. Passengers must be briefed not to use affected door.
f. All passenger seats halfway to the next exit in each direction from the inoperative door, across the entire width of the airplane, shall be blocked off with conspicuous tapes or ropes that contrast with the airplane interior before loading passengers. Only the seats in these areas shall be blocked; main passenger aisles, cross aisles and exit areas must not be blocked. (For an inoperative forward door/slide, the blocked seating area shall extend from the forward cabin end, rearward to a line halfway between the inoperative forward door and the next set of doors aft of the inoperative one. For an inoperative rear door/slide, the blocked seating area shall extend forward from the aft cabin end to a line halfway between the inoperative door and the next set of doors forward of the inoperative one).
g. Conspicuous signs and placards shall be placed in appropriate locations to indicate seats are not to be occupied by passengers.
h. Seated capacity must not exceed rated capacity of remaining pairs of exits.
i. For extended overwater operations, occupancy shall not exceed the normal rated capacity of the slide/rafts, or the remaining slide/rafts, or the rated overload capacity of the slide/rafts remaining after loss of one additional slide/raft of greatest capacity, whichever is least.
j. It is not reasonably practicable to repair the inoperative exit before the commencement of flight.
k. Repairs are made within 1 calendar day. NOTE 1: Weight and Balance Manifest must be revised as necessary to ensure proper loading limits are observed. NOTE 2: Cabin attendants may be stationed in the vicinity of each door within blocked areas. NOTE 3: A door with an inoperative EPAS must be considered inoperative.
52-11-01-01A.maintenanceNote: Cover associated signs and lights, and block associated doors and seats AMM 52-00-00/901). NOTE: If a passenger entry door’s Emergency Power Assist System (EPAS) is inoperative, the associated entry door is considered inoperative.

52-11-02.remarks:
One forward or aft stop per door (10 stops per airplane) may be missing or inoperative provided:
a. There are no visible defects on remaining stops for the affected door(s).
b. Both cabin altitude auto controllers operate normally.
c. For inoperative or missing pressure stops 1, 2, 7 and 8, limit maximum cabin differential pressure to 2.5 psi.
d. For inoperative or missing pressure stops 3, 4, 5 and 6, limit maximum cabin differential pressure to 5.4 psi.
52-11-02.maintenanceNote: Visually inspect remaining pressure stops on affected door(s) and door frame(s) to ensure there are no other defects (AMM 52-00-00/901). NOTE: Door stops are numbered 1 to 8 from bottom to top on both forward and aft edges of door.
52-11-02.operationsNote:
Airplane altitude is limited as follows to assure maximum cabin differential pressure (Delta P) limit is not exceeded by automatic cabin pressure control.
1. Before takeoff, set the landing altitude to 8000 feet.
2. For a maximum Delta P of
2.5 psi, do not exceed 14,500 feet airplane pressure altitude.
3. For a maximum Delta P of
5.4 psi, do not exceed 24,500 feet airplane pressure altitude.
4. At top of descent, reset the landing altitude to the actual field elevation for the destination airport.

52-51-02-05.title: Boeing Enhanced Flight Deck Security Door Automatic Locking System (Passenger)...............................2.52-51-02.1 - Pressure Rate-Of-Change Sensing Module
52-51-02-05.remarks:
a. Pressure sensing module is deactivated.

52-51-02-05.maintenanceNote:
Deactivate the pressure sensing module (pressure sensor) (AMM 52-00-00/901).
1. Open P110 panel F/D DR LOCK circuit breaker.
2. Remove the pressure sensor.
3. Disconnect the electrical connector from the pressure sensor.
4. A closed circuit from the pressure sensor is required to keep the automatic locking system operating. A. Fabricate a shorting plug using a connector part number equivalent to Government Designation M83513/04-A01N (detail specification MIL- DTL-83513). B. Trim the excess wire to a 2 to 3 inch length. C. Splice wires 4 and 6 together. D. Insulate splice and wire pigtails. E. Connect the shorting plug to the electrical connector and stow.
5. Install the pressure sensor.
6. Close P110 panel F/D DR LOCK circuit breaker.

52-71-01.remarks: May be inoperative provided associated door is verified closed, latched and locked before each departure.

52-71-01.operationsNote:
1. The procedures to deactivate inoperative passenger entry door sensors and forward, aft and main deck cargo (777F only) door sensors are provided to prevent unexpected display of the CONFIG DOORS warning and potential RTO due to intermittent door sensor faults.
2. The DOOR WING SLIDE L and DOOR WING SLIDE R advisory messages (-300/-300ER) and the DOOR BULK CARGO advisory message may be displayed both on the ground and in flight.
3. For doors with inoperative sensors deactivated: A. The respective door indication status message (if applicable) may be displayed both on the ground and in flight. B. Inoperative door advisory messages may be displayed on the ground only, except the DOOR BULK CARGO advisory message, which may be displayed both on the ground and in flight. C. The DOOR MAIN DECK CARGO, DOOR FWD CARGO and DOOR AFT CARGO (if applicable) caution messages may be displayed on the ground.
4. The CONFIG DOORS warning is not displayed for bulk cargo door switch faults. The following messages may be displayed after landing if the associated door sensor was deactivated: CAUTION - DOOR FWD CARGO CAUTION - DOOR AFT CARGO ADVISORY - DOOR ENTRY 1L ADVISORY - DOOR ENTRY 1R ADVISORY - DOOR AFT CARGO ADVISORY - DOOR FWD CARGO ADVISORY - DOOR E/E ACCESS COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE The 777 uses "all doors closed" logic to trigger the ACARS OOOI time stamp. 73-21-02-02-02.title: Electronic Engine Controls (EEC) Normal Mode........................................................2.73-21-02.1 - 777-300ER
73-21-02-02-02.remarks:
Normal (NORM) mode may be inoperative provided:
a. Autothrottle system operates normally.
b. LPT Turbine Case Cooling Air Flow Systems on both engines operate normally.
c. Both engines are operated in the alterative (ALTN) mode.
d. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
73-21-02-02-02.operationsNote:
NOTE 1: Derated and/or reduced thrust takeoffs, and takeoff thrust bumps are not allowed. NOTE 2: Thrust rating protection is not provided in alternate mode (for manual thrust settings) and maximum rated thrust is reached at a thrust lever position less than full forward. NOTE 3: Use of autothrottles when dispatching with EECs in alternate mode makes it easier to maintain thrust at the reference limit.
1. For EDTO flight planning, increase the engine inoperative Critical Fuel Reserves by
1.2%.
2. Base performance on EECs operating in alternate mode
3. Position both EEC Mode switches to ALTN.
4. Selection of TOB (if available) is not allowed. Select TO for takeoff.
5. For takeoff, engage autothrottles and arm VNAV. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

c. Both engines are operated in the alternate (ALTN) mode.
d. Appropriate performance adjustments are applied.
73-21-02-03.operationsNote:
NOTE 1: Derated and/or reduced thrust takeoffs, and takeoff thrust bumps are not allowed. NOTE 2: Thrust rating protection is not provided in alternate mode (for manual thrust settings) and maximum rated thrust is reached at a thrust lever position less than full forward.
1. Base performance on EECs operating in alternate mode.
2. Position both EEC Mode switches to ALTN.
3. For THRUST ASYM COMP advisory and status messages displayed, position the THRUST ASYM COMP switch to OFF then to AUTO to restore Thrust Asymmetry Compensation functionality.
4. For takeoff, advance thrust levers to approximately 50% N1, engage autothrottles and arm VNAV. COMPANY OPERATIONS NOTE This is an OPT MEL item.

80-11-01.title: Engine Start Valves
80-11-01.remarks:
One may be inoperative provided:
a. Inoperative valve is closed.
b. Alternate starting procedures are established and used.
80-11-01.maintenanceNote:
Manually open and close the valve as directed by the flight crew (AMM 80-00-00/901). For GE: (AMM 80-00-00/901)
1. Gain access to the starter air valve manual control handle by opening associated engine center thrust reverser latch access panel (415JB for left engine or 425JB right engine).
1. Unstow the starter air valve manual control handle.
2. Establish communications with the flight crew.
3. Upon command from the flight crew, engage the starter air valve manual control handle, turn the starter air valve to the open position (clockwise - one and one-quarter turns) and hold. Wear goggles, gloves and protective clothing.
4. Upon command from the flight crew, close the starter air valve.
5. When the manual override start is complete, stow the starter air valve manual control handle and close the center thrust reverser latch access panel. For RR: (AMM 80-00-00/901)
1. Gain access to the manual override start port located on the left fan cowl panel.
2. Establish communications with the flight crew.
3. Upon command from the flight crew, insert the manual start square drive in the manual override start port, turn the starter air valve to the open position and hold. Wear goggles, gloves and protective clothing.
4. Upon command from the flight crew, close the starter air valve.
5. When the manual override start is complete, remove the manual override square drive from the manual override start port.
80-11-01.operationsNote:
1. Start the associated engine using normal engine start (Autostart) procedures, with directions to ground crew for manually opening and closing the inoperative engine start valve. A. Establish communications with ground crew. B. Position engine start selector to START and advise ground crew to open start valve. C. Advise ground crew to close start valve as follows: For GE: 1) 62% N2 For RR: 2) 50% N3
2. Confirm the ENGINE STARTER CUTOUT L/R caution message is not displayed after engine start. NOTE: If the ENGINE STARTER CUTOUT L/R caution message is displayed after engine start, the starter air valve may not be closed. The starter air valve must be closed for dispatch.
3. For inflight start of the associated engine, use a windmilling start.

80-11-03.title: Start Selector Holding/Cutout Systems
80-11-03.remarks: May be inoperative provided alternate start procedures are used.
80-11-03.operationsNote:
MAINTENANCE NOTE
For AIMS status displayed due to certain failure modes of the start selector
holding/cutout relay, the AIMS status message must be cleared using the
following procedure.
1. Remove power from both AIMS cabinets by opening P11 panel AIMS L-1,
AIMS L-2, AIMS L-3, AIMS L-4, AIMS R-1, AIMS R-2, AIMS R-3 and AIMS
R-4 circuit breakers.
2. Remove the Cargo Fire/Engine Control Module (M80001) from the P5
panel without disconnecting the electrical connectors (AMM 26-22-04/401).
3. Disconnect, cap and stow the associated engine start selector wire:
A. For the left engine:
1) Disconnect electrical connector DS80100 from selector S80100.
2) For Engine Control Panel (P5) start selector with a CON position,
remove, cap and stow wire W1051-0557-24 from pin 7.
3) For Engine Control Panel (P5) start selector without a CON
position, remove, cap and stow wire W1051-0557-24 from pin 2.
4) Re-install electrical connector DS80100 on selector S80100.
B. For the right engine:
1) Disconnect electrical connector DS80200 from selector S80200.
2) For Engine Control Panel (P5) start selector with a CON position,
remove, cap and stow wire W1052-0557-24 from pin 7.
3) For Engine Control Panel (P5) start selector without a CON
position, remove, cap and stow wire W1052-0557-24 from pin 2.
4) Re-install electrical connector DS80200 on selector S80200.
4. Re-install the Cargo Fire/Engine Control Module (M80001) on the P5 panel
(AMM 26-22-04/401).
NOTE: It is only necessary to do the installation test for the Engine Start
panel. However, if any module electrical connectors were
disconnected other than the START/IGNITION or START
selector connector, then the associated installation test should be
accomplished.
5. Restore power to the AIMS cabinets by closing P11 panel AIMS L-1, AIMS
L-2, AIMS L-3, AIMS L-4, AIMS R-1, AIMS R-2, AIMS R-3 and AIMS R-4
circuit breakers.
6. Verify that the AIMS status message has cleared and no additional status
messages associated with the Cargo Fire/Engine Control Module are
displayed.
7. For engine starting, the start selector must be manually held in the START
position.

Manually open and close the associated engine start valve.
1. Position start selector to START and hold if required. For GE: Position START selector to NORM at 62% N2. For RR: Position START selector to NORM at 50% N3. Confirm the ENGINE STARTER CUTOUT L/R caution message is not displayed after engine start. NOTE: If the ENGINE STARTER CUTOUT L/R caution message is displayed after engine start, the starter air valve may not be closed. The starter air valve must be closed for dispatch.
